articles.title: Bambu Lab R1 Review: This one stands alone
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
Great hardware combined with Bambu’s excellent software and smooth user interface puts this laser among the best. The 55W CO2 laser cutter and engraver makes quick work of wood, acrylic, glass, and more.
Pros
- +Easy to assemble
- +Simple to calibrate
- +Great camera accuracy
- +Smaller footprint than other lasers in its class
- +Bambu Suite software
- +Great price
Cons
- -Optional lens required for thicker material
- -Limited material presets listed
- -Loud fans
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Bambu Lab has swung for the fences with its second go at making a laser cutter, and this time, it knocked it out of the park. The Bambu Lab R1 is a standalone, 55W CO2 laser with a roomy 600 x 300 mm work area, a bird’s eye camera for remote positioning, and a well-designed software suite. Priced at $2,499, the laser is a steal compared to other CO2 lasers of the same size and caliber.
You might recall the company’s first laser, a 40w diode packaged inside the H2D, was met with skepticism. Though the company pitched the H2D as the ultimate mini manufacturing machine for makers, many people felt a laser was too dirty to house in the same box as an expensive Core XY printer. Bambu must be listening, because they took everything that was good about the H2D’s diode system and gave it a standalone case with a massive CO2 laser.
The R1 has the same simple unboxing and setup experience as a Bambu Lab printer, making it easy to get started without a ton of prior experience. The only thing it is currently lacking is a more comprehensive set of material presets. Bambu Suite really shines in a market where good hardware is often let down by bad software.
While the Bambu Lab R1 is not a small machine, it does have a smaller footprint than other lasers with a similar work area. It requires a stout work table – and two people to cart it into position – as the machine is over 70 pounds. In its base configuration the R1 has a work area of 600mm x 300mm. With the optional conveyor and riser base, that 300mm can be extended to 3000mm, or 9.8 feet. Of course, you’ll need a lot of space in front of and behind the machine to pull that off. Bambu Lab did a wonderful job putting all of the controls and frequently used ports near the front of the R1 since you won’t want to move it much unless you are lasering something large.
The only flaw I found was the need to manually change focus lenses to cut thicker material. The process to change lenses is tedious, with six screws needing to be removed and replaced with the new lens. The two screws for the toolhead cover are ridiculously small. This process is reminiscent of the early Bambu Lab printer nozzles that required the heater and thermistor to be detached, then reinstalled with thermal paste. Hopefully Bambu Lab will come up with a quick-release lens at some point in the future.
Specifications: Bambu Lab R1
| Machine Footprint | 940 x 560 x 200 mm (37 x 22 x 7.8 inches) | 
| Machine Weight | 33.5 kg (73.8 lbs) | 
| Engraving Size | 600 x 300 mm (23.6 x 11.8 inches) With Conveyor 600 x 3000 mm (23.6 x 118.1 inches) | 
| Material | Cuts wood, acrylic (incl. clear acrylic), leather, fabric, paper, EVA foam, and shell. | 
| Engraves | The above plus coated metal, glass, and ceramic | 
| Laser Type | CO2 | 
| Laser Power | 55W | 
| Laser Wave Length | 10600 nm | 
| Engraving Accuracy | 0.10 mm | 
| Cutting Platform | Metal slats and baseplate included | 
| Connectivity | USB, Wi-Fi | 
| Interface | Color touch screen | 
| MSRP | $2,499 | 
| Release Date | September 22, 2026 | 
Bambu Lab R1: Included in the Box
The Bambu Lab R1 arrives fully assembled with its accessory pack bundled inside the laser enclosure. Accessories include a tool kit, exhaust hose, ventilation fan, antifreeze, funnel, laser alignment sensor, calibration board, and a material pack of basswood plywood and clear acrylic. You will need to supply 1500ml of distilled water to dilute the antifreeze. For the review, we also received the medium and long focus lenses, the conveyor and the riser needed for its use, the auto fire extinguishing system, and a smoke purifier.
Design of the Bambu Lab R1
The Bambu Lab R1 is a beast of a machine, but a well-thought-out one. It’s more compact than other CO2 lasers with the same working area, despite this, weighing over 70lbs. It’s not an easy machine to move. Bambu Lab put all of the controls, ports, and the safety key thoughtfully within easy reach at the front of the machine. The color touchscreen and start button are on top of the machine.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The automatic fire extinguisher ports, USB-C, and safety key are located on the left side of the laser.
The emergency stop button is located on the right side of the laser.
Only the power switch, the exhaust fan, and the coolant filling point are located on the rear of the unit.
Unlike most other lasers, a CO2 laser has a large, glass, liquid-cooled laser tube at the rear of the unit. Antifreeze is mixed with distilled water for the coolant to prevent the glass tube from freezing should it be kept in a garage, basement or even if you lose power in your house during the winter.
The laser fires a beam which is directed to the tool head with mirrors.
On some lasers, calibrating these mirrors can be a chore. Bambu Lab developed a laser alignment sensor, which clips to the toolhead and allows the laser to align the mirrors itself in just about a minute.
The Bambu Lab R1 has an excellent positioning system. There is a bird's eye camera on the lid of the laser, which requires that the lid be up when measuring. This takes a little getting used to since I reflexively shut the lid of a laser when I walk away from it. There is a camera mounted on the toolhead as well as a distance-measuring laser, instead of a clunky mechanical probe. The R1 tracks the toolhead position with XY encoders. The system worked great out of the box with no camera calibration needed. The camera is listed as having a .2mm positioning accuracy.
The Bambu Lab R1 is rated to cut up to 18mm wood and 20mm acrylic but doing so requires changing the focus lens in the tool head and then doing a five minute vision accuracy calibration. To change lenses, you need to remove two extremely tiny 1.5mm screws from the toolhead cover and four screws from the focus lens. It would be nice if they could develop a quick release for the lens, since as it is, this is not a process I’d want to have to do frequently.
A built-in air assist works to keep charring down and keep the laser lens clear. It is not adjustable, being either on or off, and it's powerful enough to move lightweight objects if they are not stuck down.
Given its size, the R1 is not likely to be used anywhere other than a shop or workroom, which is great because this thing is loud. The cooling fans in the laser don’t ever stop, and they are pretty loud on their own. When the laser is activated, it sounds like a jet engine spooling up. Between the noise of the laser and the air purification, it’s the loudest laser I’ve reviewed.
Assembling the Bambu Lab R1
The Bambu Lab R1 is fully assembled out of the box. Setup requires removing the accessory box, removing a cage around the tool head, and removing two stops holding the XY carriage in place for shipping. At initial power up the printer walks you through these steps from the touch screen.
There is a short calibration routine that automatically calibrates the laser’s mirrors by clipping the laser alignment sensor to the toolhead. In no time at all, you are ready to go.
The riser base comes in four large assemblies that are screwed together. You need to remove the base plate from the laser before setting it atop the riser. A data cable runs from the laser to the riser base, and requires deft hands to attach. Rubber feet on the bottom of the main laser unit hold it the correct position
The laser is cooled with a mixture of distilled water and antifreeze, which is poured into the rear of the laser with an included funnel. Pay close attention to the instruction booklet when adding coolant. The instructions call for “preparing” 1500ml of distilled water, then adding antifreeze to an indicated level on the rear sight window. But what it means is to pour in the antifreeze, then add as much of the 1500ml of water as needed to hit the correct level. Getting this backward makes a bit of a mess. After mopping up, I added the correct amount of water and coolant to the laser. The coolant must be topped off after turning the laser on, so don’t move the laser into a position where you cannot access the coolant port until you do this.
Safety Precautions for the Bambu Lab R1
The Bambu Lab R1 is a fully enclosed and safe Class 1 laser by itself. When running with the riser base and conveyor, it moves to a Class 4 laser. Operating a Class 4 laser requires laser-safe glasses that are not provided with the laser. I was not able to see any leakage of laser light through the riser base, but it is unavoidable when running with the conveyor. Laser light can cause severe damage to eyes and skin, and care should be taken to keep small children and pets away while the laser is in use.
The R1 has a number of built-in safety features. There is an equipment key preinstalled on the left side of the laser. When not in use this key can be pulled to prevent unauthorized access. The laser will not operate with the enclosure’s lid up and will quickly pause the job if the lid is raised while in use. If there is a problem with the job, the machine can be stopped from the touch screen, and for major problems, there is a red kill switch on the right side of the machine, which will quickly cut power to the machine completely. The laser has flame sensors which will stop the job if they detect any issues. Bambu Lab provided its optional auto fire-extinguishing system for the review. This unit has a replaceable gas canister and plugs into the left side of the laser.
Even with a good air purifier, some materials should not be burned with a laser due to their chemical makeup. Dallas Maker Space has published a list of safe and hazardous materials to use with their laser. The list of no-nos includes some plastics like PVC, fiberglass, and certain types of foams.
Software for the Bambu Lab R1
Bambu Suite was developed to run the lasers on the H series and also handle the cutting function on H2 and A2 printers. It might be the easiest to use laser software I’ve seen. The laser is connected to Wi-Fi from the touchscreen, and Bambu Suite connects to it just like a 3D printer. You import whatever you want to cut or engrave, choose the process type, hit Prepare, then select Measure, line up your art with the material, and pick the material you are using. Finally, you press Make and off it goes.
The only thing that the software doesn’t have is a large list of default materials. The basics are there, but hopefully more will be added over time. As it is, a number of the projects I did required internet searches and guesswork to find material settings that worked.
Makerworld is accessible directly from Bambu Suite, and it has an expanding group of shared laser projects to help you get started.
Engraving / Cutting with the Bambu Lab R1
For the first job, we used the test file from Bambu Lab that includes line drawing, engraving, and cutting on 3 mm basswood plywood. The test file did not list the settings, but the overall job took under two minutes to complete and looks really good. The cuts show much less charring than you would see on a diode laser.
Next, I tried a really intricate butterfly decoration from PabloLab on Makerworld.com. Using the default material settings for 3mm basswood, 75% power at 30 mm/s, the cut was perfect. The butterfly and the interior cuts dropped out of the material with no weeding needed. I should point out I broke off one of her antennae in handling.
The Bambu Lab R1 is rated to cut up to 18mm black walnut and 20mm acrylic, but the thicker wood requires the optional medium or long focus lenses. I tested cutting on a piece of pine lumber that is 19.5mm thick but is much softer than black walnut. There was no material default for anything thicker than 3mm. The cut on the left used the long focus lens and did the best cut at the lowest power, using 80% power at 10mm/s and 4 passes. The cut in the middle used the medium focus lens at 85% power at 5 mm/s and required 5 passes. The short focus lens really did not totally punch through the bottom of the material. The cuts are charred due to using 100% power at 4 mm/s through multiple tries.
For cutting out stickers out of sheets of sticker paper, we used the material preset for 200g kraft paper, 45% power at 250mm/s. The cuts were perfect and only took a few seconds. With a jig mounted on the cutting plate, the results are repeatable page after page.
There was no material preset for PETG so with a little trial and error we stepped that down to 65% power at 35mm/s for 2mm PETG and 20% power at 20mm/s for 1mm PETG. With air assist, the results were terrific, with just a very little smoke cloudiness at the edges of the PETG cuts. At these speeds, the cuts all took less than a minute.
Where most lasers just pass right through clear materials, CO2 lasers run at a high enough frequency to cut and engrave them. Using the shape library in Bambu Suite for the designs, we cut a bunch of blanks for use with our UV printer out of clear PETG sheets and clear acrylic. The material settings in Bambu Suite were perfect for 3mm clear acrylic at 80% power at 10mm/s speed.
CO2 lasers can also engrave glass with no masking needed, though a thin smear of liquid soap is suggested to keep chipping down. There was no material preset for glass, so a quick internet search led to settings from a competitor’s 55-watt CO2 laser. Using 30% power and 250mm/s, with air assist on, the engraving took just seconds and looks excellent.
CO2 lasers can’t cut metal, but they do a good job engraving coated metal. The Bambu lab R1has a curved surface machining mode for curved surfaces like this flask and tumblers. The auto measure function creates a 3D map of the material’s surface and shows the engravable area. Using the settings for aluminum business cards, 70% power at 400mm/s, the job took less than a minute and looks sharp and clear.
Bottom Line
The Bambu Lab R1 is an impressive step into the laser market. Good hardware with even better software makes the R1 an excellent choice for makers and small businesses needing an easy-to-use CO2 laser. It’s simple enough for a beginner to use, leaving you with more time to focus on making art, not fussing over settings.
Retailing at $2,499, the R1 is more expensive than a hobby-level diode, but a downright bargain compared to the competition. If you’re serious about making cool things or running a small business, the price is worth it.
By combining a 55W CO2, a generous 600 x 300 mm work area, and automated mirror calibration, it delivers high-grade cutting performance through wood, acrylic, and glass with minimal charring. While the manual lens swap process is a minor hassle and the operational noise requires a dedicated workspace or shop environment, its performance outclasses most competitors in its price range.
If you’re not ready to invest in a professional-grade machine, check out the Creality Falcon A1 Pro, a very capable 20W for $1,099. If you’re thinking about engraving glass or handling materials without charring, the xTool F2 Ultra UV is a great “cold” laser that runs for $4,299. If you want to take your laser with you, a portable xTool F1 laser is a heck of a deal at $819.
Denise Bertacchi is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware US, covering 3D printing. Denise has been crafting with PCs since she discovered Print Shop had clip art on her Apple IIe. She loves reviewing 3D printers because she can mix all her passions: printing, photography, and writing.

articles.title: Microsoft disrupts AI-assisted platform that compromised 12,000 accounts
articles.text:
Microsoft said Tuesday that it led an industry-wide disruption of a subscription-based scam platform that used an AI chatbot to compromise 12,000 Microsoft accounts over a few-month span.
Named EvilTokens, the platform was introduced over a Telegram channel in February and charged an initial $1,500 fee and a recurring $500 charge each month after that. EvilTokens provided a single service for streamlining most steps required to compromise email accounts in large numbers. From there, the platform helped customers analyze inboxes, select targets that would provide the biggest potential payouts, and draft follow-up emails that provided realistic ruses for tricking company employees into transferring funds to attacker-controlled accounts.
Minutes, not days
“While EvilTokens helped cybercriminals access email accounts, at the center of the service was an AI-style chatbot that could analyze a victim’s inbox and help criminals identify trusted relationships, payment authorizations, and sensitive responsibilities, as well as other circumstances where fraud was most likely to succeed,” Microsoft said. “The platform could even recommend fraud strategies, including drafting messages that impersonated trusted contacts to help criminals trick victims into taking action.”
Microsoft said users of EvilToken compromised 12,000 customer accounts belonging to 10,000 organizations around the world, with the highest concentration of them located in the US. Countries with the next-largest numbers were Canada, the UK, Australia, India, and France. Victim organizations included wholesale distribution, construction, financial services, real estate, higher education, and healthcare. SpyCloud, a security firm that assisted in the disruption operation, has more details about victims here.
Using a legal process and a network of partners, Microsoft seized 50 websites and 150 more domains used to operate EvilTokens. The UK’s Metropolitan Police Service arrested two men on suspicion of offenses allegedly connected to the crime platform.
Account compromises were achieved through a legitimate OAuth process known as device code authentication. This form of authentication is designed for TVs and input-constrained devices, meaning those that lack the interface for performing normal log-in processes. In this model, the device being signed into presents a code and instructs the user to enter it into a browser on a separate device. The new device is then authenticated.

articles.title: Goodram Expands Its Gaming-Focused RIVAL Series With RIVAL Charge DDR5 Memory
articles.text:
Tuesday, September 22nd 2026
	
	
	
	
Goodram Expands Its Gaming-Focused RIVAL Series With RIVAL Charge DDR5 Memory
Goodram is expanding its gaming-focused RIVAL series with RIVAL Charge DDR5 memory. The new DIMM modules are designed for computers based on DDR5 platforms, including both new systems and upgraded configurations. The series includes variants with speeds of up to 6800 MT/s and latencies starting from CL30, as well as kits with a total capacity of up to 64 GB.
Gaming today is about more than just the game
A game, Discord, a browser with multiple tabs, gameplay recording, streaming and system monitoring—in a modern gaming configuration, RAM rarely serves just one application.RIVAL Charge DDR5 was designed with exactly this kind of workload in mind. Higher memory bandwidth is beneficial when multiple operations are running in parallel, while the right capacity gives the system more headroom when several demanding applications are active at the same time.
That is why RIVAL Charge lets users choose not only the frequency and latency, but also the capacity that best reflects how the computer is actually used.
6800 MT/s makes an impression. But it is not the only number that matters
When choosing DDR5 memory, it is easy to focus primarily on frequency. However, the MT/s figure alone does not tell the whole story about a module's performance characteristics. Latency, specified among others by CAS Latency (CL), is equally important. RIVAL Charge will be available in 5600 and 6000 MT/s configurations with latencies starting from CL30, 6400 MT/s CL32, and 6800 MT/s CL34. Selected CL36 variants will also be available.
This broad range makes it possible to match the memory to the capabilities of the processor and motherboard instead of reducing the choice to the highest available MT/s value. When building a computer, the entire set of parameters matters—speed, latency, compatibility and capacity.
The capacity range is equally broad. RIVAL Charge will be available as individual 8, 16 and 32 GB modules, as well as dual-channel kits: 2 × 8 GB, 2 × 16 GB and 2 × 32 GB. This makes it possible to build configurations ranging from 16 GB for less demanding systems, through a versatile 32 GB for gaming and multitasking, up to 64 GB for users who game, stream, edit content or work with more demanding applications on the same computer.
DDR5 for where a new configuration begins
RIVAL Charge expands the Goodram RIVAL family with a solution designed for DDR5 platforms. Existing RIVAL DDR4 modules remain an option for users upgrading computers based on the older standard without having to replace the processor and motherboard.
RIVAL Charge, on the other hand, is aimed at new and upgraded configurations using DDR5. The range from 5600 to 6800 MT/s makes it possible to choose memory for both more straightforward gaming PCs and higher-performance systems also used for streaming or content creation.Profiles instead of manual parameter tuning
RIVAL Charge supports Intel XMP 3.0 and AMD EXPO profiles. On a compatible platform, they allow users to apply predefined frequency, latency and voltage settings without having to configure each parameter manually.
After selecting the appropriate profile in the BIOS, the user can activate settings prepared for a specific memory variant. This is particularly useful for those who want to take advantage of the modules' capabilities without manually configuring individual DRAM parameters.
Red is only the beginning
The first RIVAL Charge modules feature a red-and-black heat spreader and a black PCB, maintaining the distinctive gaming aesthetic of the RIVAL family. This color variant is only the beginning, however—Goodram plans to expand the RIVAL Charge line with additional color options, giving users greater freedom to match the memory to the overall look of their system.
This is particularly relevant in computers where components increasingly form part of the visual design—from the color of the case and cooling system to the motherboard, cables and other components. Design, however, does not come at the expense of compatibility. The modules are 32.85 mm high, and their low-profile design makes them easier to use in configurations with larger CPU coolers, where space above the DIMM slots may be limited.
Like other Goodram RIVAL memory modules, RIVAL Charge DDR5 is covered by the manufacturer's lifetime warranty.

articles.title: Code statt Labor: Wie KI das Problem bitterer Pflanzenproteine angeht
articles.text:
Gegen den fiesen Geschmack: Wie eine KI die Bitterkeit aus Pflanzenproteinen rechnet
Ein Forschungsteam des Leibniz-Instituts für Lebensmittel-Systembiologie an der Technischen Universität München im bayerischen Freising hat eine KI-basierte Methode zur strukturellen Analyse von Geschmacksstoffen entwickelt. Wie aus einer im Fachmagazin npj Science of Food veröffentlichten Studie hervorgeht, kann das System die Bitterkeit von Peptiden präzise vorhersagen und neue molekulare Strukturen gezielt am Computer generieren.
Kombination aus Sprachmodell und neuronalem Netz
Die Wissenschaftlerinnen um Antonella Di Pizio kombinierten für ihre Untersuchung ein Protein-Sprachmodell mit dem sogenannten BitterPep-GCN. Dabei handelt es sich um ein künstliches neuronales Netz in Form eines Graph Convolutional Networks, das in der Bioinformatik primär für die Auswertung komplex strukturierter Daten eingesetzt wird.
Das Sprachmodell ZymCTRL, welches ursprünglich für die Untersuchung biologischer Enzyme konzipiert wurde, erfasste anhand von knapp 500 bekannten, bitter schmeckenden Peptiden die spezifischen molekularen Muster. Durch diesen sogenannten Transfer-Learning-Ansatz erzeugte das System eigenständig 161 neue Peptidsequenzen, die das BitterPep-GCN-Modell im nächsten Schritt hinsichtlich ihrer chemischen Struktur filterte und bewertete.
Die Analysen zeigten dabei, dass oft schon sehr kurze Aminosäureketten für messbare geschmackliche Reaktionen verantwortlich sind. Ein konkretes Beispiel dafür ist eine Verbindung aus drei Tryptophan-Molekülen. Da diese Aminosäure in der Biochemie mit dem Buchstaben W abgekürzt wird, trägt das Konstrukt die Bezeichnung Tripeptid WWW.
Diese kurze Kette aktiviert die Bitter-Rezeptoren auf der menschlichen Zunge besonders stark. Die sogenannte sensorische Schwelle liegt hier bei 4,1 Mikromol pro Liter. Das bedeutet, dass die Testpersonen den bitteren Geschmack bereits bei dieser äußerst geringen Konzentration in einer Lösung deutlich wahrnehmen konnten.
Synthese und Überprüfung im Labor
Um die theoretischen Berechnungen in der Praxis zu verifizieren, ließ das Team die vielversprechendsten Kandidaten der simulierten Peptide synthetisieren. Ein geschultes Sensorik-Panel aus zwölf menschlichen Testpersonen verkostete diese Substanzen anschließend unter standardisierten Bedingungen, um die tatsächlichen Geschmacksschwellen der künstlich generierten Stoffe zu ermitteln.
Die praktische Überprüfung bestätigte die algorithmischen Vorhersagen weitgehend, da die Testpersonen 25 von 31 Peptiden korrekt als bitter oder nicht-bitter einstuften. Die Erstautorin der Studie, die Doktorandin Alexandra Steuer, konstatiert laut Phys.org, dass das Verfahren nicht nur Vorhersagen treffe, sondern die aktive Konstruktion neuer bitter schmeckender Peptide ermögliche.
Neben der reinen Bestimmung von Bitterkeit registrierte das Panel bei vier der als bitter verifizierten Peptide bei höheren Konzentrationen eine zusätzliche saure Geschmacksnote. Die Forscher:innen führen diesen Effekt auf das Vorhandensein von Glutaminsäure innerhalb der Peptidketten zurück, die in der organischen Chemie als bekannter Determinant für sauren Geschmack gilt.
Relevanz für die Lebensmittelproduktion
Bitter schmeckende Peptide entstehen vorrangig beim enzymatischen oder chemischen Abbau von Proteinen. In der Praxis ist das ein allgegenwärtiges Phänomen. Werden etwa alltägliche fermentierte Produkte wie Kefir, Parmesan oder Bergkäse hergestellt, bilden sich genau diese geschmacklichen Fehlnoten, ebenso wie bei der Produktion moderner Proteinpulver. Die exakte Identifikation dieser molekularen Auslöser ist eine Voraussetzung, um die Bitterkeit bei industriellen Verarbeitungsprozessen künftig gezielt zu kontrollieren.
Die Studienleiterin Antonella Di Pizio erklärt, dass diese neuen Erkenntnisse langfristig helfen könnten, den Geschmack pflanzlicher, proteinreicher Lebensmittel systematisch zu steuern. „Um pflanzliche Proteinquellen für die Lebensmittelproduktion attraktiver zu machen und nachhaltiger zu nutzen, müssen wir besser verstehen, welche Peptide bitter schmecken und welche Strukturmerkmale sie auszeichnen“, so die Forscherin.
Trotz der methodischen Ergebnisse weisen solche datengetriebenen Modelle Abhängigkeiten auf, da sie zwingend große Mengen experimentell gesicherter Trainingsdaten benötigen. Wenn die grundlegende Datenbank nicht hinreichend ausbalanciert ist, können die künstlichen neuronalen Netze spezifische Rezeptor-Bindungen nur eingeschränkt abbilden, was die Trefferquote bei komplexeren Proteinketten potenziell verringert. Hat das Modell beispielsweise fast ausschließlich mit kurzen Aminosäureketten aus der Fermentation von Parmesan oder Kefir trainiert, fehlt ihm schlichtweg die Datengrundlage, um die gänzlich anders aufgebauten, wesentlich längeren Bitterstoffe in einem neuartigen Erbsen- oder Haferproteinprodukt korrekt vorherzusagen.

articles.title: Qualcomm reveals Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, its most powerful SoC ever [benchmark update]
articles.text:
Snapdragon flew me out to Hawaii to check out its latest chip, the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and, for the first time ever, the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, the company’s premier “extreme-levelled” mobile chipset.
We did live benchmarking with Geekbench 6 and saw a single-core score of 4,293 and a multi-core score of 12,924. We also used Geekbench 7 and had a single-core score of 3,608 and a multi-core score of 12,257.
The Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 series has a reengineered Qualcomm Hexagon NPU that allows the Elite Gen 6’s agentic AI features to comprehend personal context across devices; it also tries to anticipate your needs, learn and adapt over time, and auto-prompt photo editing. The Elite Extreme has more advanced agentic AI with deeper contextual understanding. Additionally, it has significantly enhanced on-device AI performance. Extreme is supposed to deliver agents faster, more personalized and more dependable.
Qualcomm says its Custom-built Oryon CPU offers industry-leading performance, with peak speeds up to 5.0GHz. Additionally, it says the CPU is fast, offering responsive experiences across play and creativity, and seamless multitasking throughout the day. The Elite Extreme has all of this plus “Snapdragon’s most powerful gaming, creation, and AI experiences.” Qualcomm also says it offers system-level contributions for an overall better-performing package. It also includes the VVC codec for more power-efficient videos.
The Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6’s next-gen Adreno GPU sports faster, smoother gameplay with intelligent graphic enhancements, as well as responsive controls, fluid reactions, and a full suite of Snapdragon 8 Elite gaming experiences. The 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, on the other hand, sports AI-dedicated Adreno matrix cores and runs advanced models. Additionally, it features Adreno Neural Fusion for AI-driven super resolution and frame generation and even has 18MB of high-performance memory.
Additionally, the 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 offers cinema-grade video with APV support, as well as 8K60 video capture and 4K240 ultra HD slow-motion.
And Qualcomm is already launching the first product with the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6: the Motorola Signature 27.
Update: 09/22/2026: We’ve done some live benchmarking of the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 added above.

articles.title: Qualcomm launches two new smartphone chips with emphasis on AI | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Qualcomm today announced two flagship smartphone processors, called Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, with a focus on facilitating better AI-focused features.
At its annual Snapdragon Summit, Qualcomm said that the new chips can aid in improved personalization for AI agents. The chips have new sensing hubs that can run small models of up to 200 million parameters. With the new sensing hub, smartphones can run a personal scribe locally and differentiate between speakers. Plus, it can build memory based on your usage for better suggestions for automating tasks. The company said that it can run a complete voice-in and voice-out agent through the new chip.
The Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 has a new accelerator element that’s designed to run models in a more efficient way. The high-end Extreme version can run a 30-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) model locally. This means that while the overall model size is 30B, the model only activates a certain number of parameters for a particular task.
For comparison, at its Worldwide Developer Conference (WWDC) in June, Apple released a 20-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model, the most advanced of its third generation of foundation models.
The new Qualcomm CPU also provides pixel-level control for cameras to facilitate more pro-level experiences, along with improved stabilization and motion understanding. The Extreme version can support video recording at 8K 60fps and at 4K240 for ultra HD slow-motion. It also enables the new Advanced Professional Video (APV) codec for pro-level recording.
What’s more, both chips can use AI to boost vocals and reduce noise. Plus, it has Qualcomm’s new voice bubble tech, which isolates users’ noise during calls.
At the event, Motorola announced its Motorola Signature 27 smartphone, powered by the Snapdragon Gen 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, with general availability sometime this year.
Qualcomm has been working on more than 40 AI devices, but there is still a belief that a lot of people will use their phones for AI rather than other dedicated devices. Nothing co-founder Carl Pei has hinted at this trend in the past, and more recently, new Apple CEO John Ternus reinforced the same line of thought during the iPhone Duo launch earlier this month.

articles.title: Hikal shareholders to vote on Sameer Hiremath’s elevation amid family ownership dispute
articles.text:
Hikal shareholders to vote on Sameer Hiremath’s elevation amid family ownership dispute
At Hikal’s AGM on September 23, shareholders will vote on Sameer Hiremath’s five-year term as CMD. The Hiremath and Kalyani sides hold nearly identical 34% stakes, while proxy advisers are split over the move.
Weeks after the Tata Sons boardroom dispute put questions of shareholder power, board authority and succession back in focus, another family-linked corporate contest is approaching a key vote.
Shareholders of Hikal Ltd will vote on Wednesday, September 23, on the appointment of Sameer Hiremath as chairman and managing director for a five-year term beginning October 1. What might otherwise have been a routine succession exercise has become a closely watched governance vote. Hikal remains caught in a decades-old ownership dispute between the Hiremath and Kalyani families, while proxy advisers have taken opposing positions on Hiremath’s elevation.
InGovern has recommended that shareholders oppose the appointment, citing concerns over combining the chairman and managing director roles under a promoter-family executive and the level of disclosure around remuneration. Institutional Investor Advisory Services (IiAS) and Stakeholders Empowerment Services (SES), however, have recommended support, citing Hiremath’s nearly three decades at Hikal and the need for leadership continuity as founder and executive chairman Jai Hiremath steps down.
Hikal is a contract development and manufacturing company with businesses spanning pharmaceuticals and crop protection, supplying products and services to global customers.
Near-equal stakes sharpen the vote
The Hiremath family holds about 34.84% of Hikal, while Kalyani Investment Co. Ltd and BF Investment Ltd together hold about 34.01%.
Public and institutional shareholders account for the remaining roughly 31%. With the two promoter sides almost evenly matched, voting patterns among the remaining shareholders could have a significant bearing on the outcome. The two families have been locked in a long-running dispute over Hikal’s ownership.
Sugandha Hiremath, sister of Bharat Forge Chairman Babasaheb ‘Baba’ Kalyani, and her husband Jai Hiremath have argued in court that a family arrangement dating back to the 1990s required Hikal shares held by Kalyani-controlled entities to eventually be transferred to the Hiremath side. The Kalyani side contests that claim.
There is no public indication yet of how the Kalyani-controlled entities intend to vote on Sameer Hiremath’s appointment. YourStory reached out to Hikal and the Kalyani side for comments. Neither had responded at the time of publication.
The leadership transition also comes after a difficult financial year. Hikal swung to a consolidated net loss of Rs 49 crore in FY26 from a profit of Rs 91 crore a year earlier, with exceptional items also weighing on the bottom line. The June quarter showed signs of improvement, with revenue rising year-on-year and the quarterly net loss narrowing to Rs 7.4 crore from Rs 22.4 crore.
More than a succession vote
The Hikal situation is structurally different from Tata Sons. Tata Sons is an unlisted holding company with its own governance framework, while Hikal is a listed company where the appointment is being put directly to shareholders. But both episodes underline how succession can become complicated when ownership, board authority and executive control sit across different centres of influence. Hikal’s AGM will be held virtually at 11:30 AM on September 23.
The vote will not resolve the Hiremath-Kalyani ownership dispute, but with the two sides holding almost identical stakes, it will provide a visible test of how shareholder power is exercised at Hikal as leadership passes from one generation to the next.

articles.title: Kantata debuts Agent Studio for building custom AI agents in plain language - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Kantata debuts Agent Studio for building custom AI agents in plain language
Professional services automation software company Kantata Inc. today unveiled Agent Studio, a tool that lets services firms build custom artificial intelligence agents by describing the job they want done in plain language.
The release goes after a problem Kantata says is building in the professional services automation market. Vendors are shipping narrow agents by the dozen, each scoped to a single job such as resourcing or risk reporting.
The company argues that every new one arrives as another silo to maintain. Kantata sells a single agent that it says carries context across the whole platform. That’s the Expertise Agent, which Kantata launched in June and calls the first AI superagent for professional services.
Agent Studio sits inside the Kantata Expertise Engine and works through conversation. A user describes the job, and the Expertise Agent assembles the new agent and refines it the same way, with every build and edit checked for correctly structured inputs and outputs before it is published.
Nobody has to fill in a form or write code. Once live, an agent can be triggered by a person or picked up automatically by a workflow on a single command.
The intended users are practice leads and delivery directors. Under Agent Studio a standard gets written down once, covering the format, the escalation rules and the outputs a recurring deliverable needs, then applied automatically rather than rebuilt by whoever happens to be staffed that week. Kantata calls the overhead it removes a “prompt tax,” the cycle of drafting and reformatting that a team repeats every time it re-explains the same job to an AI tool.
“When it comes to professional services, AI isn’t the differentiator — expertise is,” Chief Executive Michael Speranza said. “Any vendor can give a firm a tool to build AI agents. But if all you’re doing is automating processes, you’re just racing to the bottom and simply reducing costs, rather than developing differentiation.”
Chief Technology Officer Vikas Nehru put the case on governance grounds, calling an agent that improvises “a liability in a business where the same deliverable has to hold up in front of a client every time.”
Finnish invoice automation company Basware Oyj uses Kantata’s software in its own professional services operation. Mark Johnston, its chief customer officer, said he wants his services team with customers rather than “doing documentation, figuring out resourcing and entering their billable time,” and that Kantata lets the firm build agents to absorb that work.
The announcement cites Forrester Research Inc. on the wider point. Ted Schadler, a vice president and principal analyst at the firm, has written that the only durable route to business advantage now runs through putting a company’s own proprietary knowledge and expertise to work in AI models, apps and agents.

articles.title: El Realme 16 Pro 5G estrena una edición especial para fans de Harry Potter con una tirada muy limitada
articles.text:
Aunque aún quedan tres meses para el estreno de la nueva serie de 'Harry Potter', los fans de la saga del famoso mago están de enhorabuena, ya que ahora la firma Realme ha lanzado una edición especial del Realme 16 Pro 5G, a la que han bautizado Harry Potter Edition. Este móvil tiene un precio de 699 euros en su versión de 12 GB de RAM y 256 GB de almacenamiento interno.
realme 16 Pro 5G Smartphone Harry Potter Edition, 12GB+256GB
Un móvil con una gran cantidad de detalles para los fans de Harry Potter
Las ediciones especiales inspiradas en franquicias icónicas corren a menudo el riesgo de quedarse en un mero cambio de carcasa con un sobreprecio injustificado. Con este nuevo modelo de Realme, la marca busca alejarse de ese enfoque superficial integrando un trabajo de diseño profundo en el chasis, un empaquetado temático repleto de coleccionables y una interfaz de usuario personalizada, todo ello manteniendo la base técnica de su gama media-alta.
En el apartado estético, el dispositivo destaca por su trasera grabada con láser en tonos oscuros que refleja el escudo de Hogwarts y motivos del universo mágico, acompañada por detalles dorados alrededor del módulo de cámaras.
El paquete incluye una caja personalizada con forma de baúl, una herramienta de extracción de SIM con la forma del escudo de la famosa escuela de magia o la carta de admisión, pegatinas y temas exclusivos para la capa de personalización de software.
En lo puramente técnico, el terminal mantiene las especificaciones del Realme 16 Pro 5G estándar. Cuenta con una pantalla AMOLED de 6,78 pulgadas con tasa de refresco a 144 Hz, un procesador de la serie MediaTek Dimensity 7300 Max 5G optimizado para la eficiencia energética y conectividad 5G.
A todo ello, se le suma además un sistema de cámaras donde cobra protagonismo un sensor principal de alta resolución de 200 MP con estabilización óptica (OIS). Todo ello respaldado por una batería de gran capacidad con sistema de carga rápida a 45 W que permite recuperar el 100% en pocos minutos.
Aunque hay algo por lo que destaca este móvil es por estrenar la primera tecnología Quadra de detección de luz y cambio de color del mundo. Esta tecnología permite disfrutar del efecto fotocromático denominado Hogwarts Crest Glow Wonder, gracias al cual los escudos de las cuatro casas delcolegio revelan sus colores característicos al exponerse a la luz del sol.

articles.title: Google Messages va avoir droit à une refonte de son moteur de recherche
articles.text:
Google Messages s’apprête à accueillir une refonte de son module de recherche. Google est en effet en train de plancher sur une nouvelle version du moteur de recherche intégré à sa messagerie pour proposer une nouvelle expérience axée sur la consultation et la navigation dans les médias partagés au sein des conversations.
Une interface de recherche plus visuelle
Concrètement, cette nouvelle page de recherche va adopter une interface bien plus visuelle qu’à l’accoutumée, en proposant d’accéder aux médias reçus à travers une grille organisée par type de fichiers avec pour chacun un aperçu. Vous pourrez ainsi accéder facilement à l’ensemble des images, vidéos ou liens reçu dans l’ensemble de vos conversations. Une manière pour Google de vous permettre de retrouver un contenu récent rapidement sans avoir à saisir la moindre recherche dans le champ prévu à cet effet.
Le champ de recherche, quant à lui, serait greffé en bas de l’écran, plutôt qu’en haut comme c’est le cas actuellement. Autre nouveauté particulièrement intéressante, ce nouveau moteur de recherche permet de rechercher plus facilement du texte dans une conversation précise. Google a également repensé l’affichage des liens et des lieux partagés dans les conversations avec un aperçu de ceux-ci plus complet.
La messagerie de Google adopte par ailleurs un visualiseur de média remis au goût du jour. L’ouverture d’une photo ou d’une vidéo depuis un résultat de recherche lance une visionneuse similaire à celle déjà en place dans les conversations RCS individuelle, avec un effet de flou en arrière-plan et un bouton de téléchargement greffé en haut à droite de l’écran plutôt qu’en bas à gauche comme c’est le cas actuellement. À noter qu’il est également possible de passer d’un contenu multimédia à un autre très facilement en swipant directement l’écran.
Toutes ces nouveautés découvertes par Android Authority, habitué à décortiquer les APK d’installation des applications Android, sont pour l’heure encore à l’état de développement. Reste désormais à patienter encore quelques semaines, voire quelques mois, pour espérer voir ces changements arriver dans une prochaine mise à jour de Google Messages, à condition, évidemment, que Google ne change pas ses plans d’ici là.

articles.title: Une Xbox Series X qui émule des jeux PS5 ? Cette démo montre que ce n’est plus totalement de la science-fiction
articles.text:
Faire tourner des jeux PS5 directement sur une Xbox Series X paraît encore relever du fantasme de bidouilleur. Pourtant, un développeur vient de montrer que l’idée n’est plus complètement absurde, avec un portage expérimental d’un émulateur PS5 sur la console de Microsoft.
Le projet s’appelle PS5X et repose sur KytyPS5, un émulateur PlayStation 5 open source déjà actif sur PC. Ici, Devran Cosmo Uenal a entrepris de le porter directement sur Xbox Series X, avec de premiers résultats suffisamment concrets pour dépasser le simple écran de démarrage.
Plusieurs jeux PS5 tournent déjà sur Xbox Series X
PS5X fonctionne via le mode développeur de la Xbox, et non dans l’environnement classique de la console. Il ne s’agit donc pas d’une application que l’on peut installer tranquillement depuis le Microsoft Store avant de lancer sa ludothèque PlayStation, Microsoft ayant largement fermé la porte aux émulateurs dans l’environnement classique de ses consoles.
Le développeur a néanmoins réussi à exécuter les versions PS5 de GEX Trilogy, Hellboy: Web of Wyrd, Marvel Cosmic Invasion et Quake II. Ces quatre jeux sont également disponibles sur d’autres plateformes : l’intérêt de la démonstration tient bien au fait que ce sont ici leurs builds PS5 qui sont exécutés par émulation sur une Xbox Series X. La manette est reconnue sur les quatre titres et le son fonctionne déjà dans certains cas.
Le vrai défi se joue entre Vulkan et DirectX
PS5 et Xbox Series X partagent certes plusieurs points communs matériels, avec des processeurs x86-64 AMD et des GPU issus de la famille RDNA 2. Cela facilite certaines choses, mais ne suffit évidemment pas à rendre leurs logiciels interchangeables.
Le principal obstacle se situe notamment du côté du rendu graphique. Sur PC, KytyPS5 s’appuie sur Vulkan. Or la Xbox ne propose pas de prise en charge native de cette API : PS5X doit donc adapter le travail graphique vers l’environnement DirectX de Microsoft. Les avancées réalisées sur la version PC de KytyPS5 ne peuvent ainsi pas être récupérées telles quelles sur Xbox.
La différence se voit d’ailleurs dans les résultats. Sur PC, KytyPS5 a récemment progressé au point de lancer des jeux 3D nettement plus complexes : GTA V atteint désormais ses menus et plusieurs autres titres commencent à afficher du gameplay, même si l’on reste très loin d’une compatibilité complète.
PS5X reste donc avant tout un projet de recherche, avec une liste de jeux compatibles minuscule et beaucoup de travail devant lui. Mais réussir à exécuter plusieurs builds PS5 directement sur une Xbox Series X constitue déjà une étape intéressante. De là à voir un jour les grosses exclusivités PlayStation tourner correctement sur la machine de Microsoft, il reste toutefois un sacré morceau de code à avaler !

articles.title: Le Rampart, la nouvelle arme anti-drones de la Marine nationale, repéré sur le Mistral avant son départ pour l'Afrique
articles.text:
C’est un équipement militaire nouveau dans les forces armées françaises, qui pourrait bien être généralisé s’il fait ses preuves lors des exercices qui lui seront soumis. Sur des photos diffusées par des comptes dédiés aux sujets militaires, une tourelle inhabituelle a été repérée sur le pont du Mistral, l’un des trois porte-hélicoptères amphibies de la Marine nationale.
Il n’a pas fallu bien longtemps aux spécialistes pour identifier cette structure installée sur le navire. Ce module est appelé Rampart : il s’agit du nouveau nom, plus spectaculaire et plus symbolique, pour désigner le lanceur modulaire polyvalent (LMP), un projet d’armement porté par Naval Group, l’un des géants de la défense en Europe.
Cette nouvelle identité, officialisée en juin au salon Eurosatory, peut toutefois faire perdre de vue l’objectif de cette initiative : disposer d’une tourelle polyvalente, capable d’accueillir des modules spécifiques pour des munitions variées. L’idée ? Avoir un seul élément capable de gérer à la volée des menaces différentes nécessitant des intercepteurs précis.
Ce printemps, un démonstrateur avait déjà tiré à Canjuers (Var), le plus grand camp militaire d’Europe occidentale, notamment des roquettes de 68 mm (guidées laser et non guidées) « dans une configuration sol-sol ». Naval Group, satisfait de cette première vague de tests, ajoutait que l’étape suivante passerait par des « essais en mer ».
Un baptême du feu en mer dans le golfe de Guinée
C’est ce qui semble se concrétiser aujourd’hui. RFI rapportait d’ailleurs, dès le 13 septembre, le prochain appareillage d’un porte-hélicoptères amphibie en direction du golfe de Guinée, au large de l’Afrique de l’Ouest, dans le cadre de la mission récurrente Corymbe. Le 14, Le Marin indiquait que le PHA en partance était bien le Mistral, celui équipé du Rampart.
D’ailleurs, Naval Group avait annoncé un premier tir en mer en octobre, à bord d’un Mistral. On parlait alors d’un essai dans le cadre de l’exercice Wildfire, exercice spécifiquement pensé à la lutte intensive anti-drones, dont la date pour l’édition 2026 n’a pas été indiquée.
Si le Rampart voyage avec le Mistral, ce n’est certainement pas un hasard : le constructeur entend profiter manifestement de ce déploiement pour l’éprouver en mer – la fameuse prochaine étape de la campagne de tirs, qui implique de nouveaux scénarios, comme faire face à des drones navals et à des menaces aériennes diverses.
Le Rampart est capable d’aligner des munitions comme des roquettes, des missiles, des grenades, des leurres et même des armes sous-marines et des drones. Sa capacité d’autodéfense rapprochée est annoncée jusqu’à huit kilomètres (et même jusqu’à dix kilomètres, avance Mer et Marine), avec le soutien d’une tonne de projectiles à bord (la « charge utile »).
L’équation économique face aux menaces asymétriques
Le lanceur modulaire polyvalent entend apporter une réponse au « contexte actuel de menaces asymétriques et protéiformes », qui met à mal la logique plus traditionnelle d’un lanceur par type d’arme. La place croissante que les drones prennent dans la guerre, le développement des essaims et l’essor de l’IA embarquée imposent de repenser la défense.
Dans le jargon militaire, Rampart appartient à la famille des systèmes de défense rapprochée (CIWS, pour Close-In Weapon Systems), ces armes de dernier recours censées stopper une attaque juste avant l’impact (le nom de Rampart, rempart en français, colle donc plutôt bien à la fonction). Et le raisonnement derrière est d’abord comptable.
En mer Rouge, la marine américaine a passé des mois à abattre des drones houthis à quelques milliers d’euros pièce en y consacrant des missiles bien plus chers que leurs cibles, un échange intenable sur la durée. Même chose d’ailleurs pour la Marine nationale ainsi que pour les autres forces navales qui ont abattu des drones adverses.
Naval Group vend justement une proposition adaptée et à bas coût : une réponse « proportionnée au coût de la menace », autrement dit une roquette bon marché pour un drone bon marché. Pour garnir la tourelle, le groupe s’appuie sur Thales et KNDS, et travaille avec MBDA sur les missiles des familles Mistral et Akeron.
Un gain de puissance de feu pour la flotte française
Un LMP comme le Rampart vient par ailleurs muscler très franchement le Mistral, dont l’armement est léger. On ne compte que 2 canons de 20 mm téléopérés, 4 mitrailleuses de 12,7 mm, et 2 systèmes d’autodéfense surface-air à très courte portée SIMBAD (missile Mistral). Certes, le PHA est censé compter sur son escorte… mais faut-il encore qu’elle soit au niveau.
De fait, le LMP a de quoi partiellement compenser ce défaut d’escorte ; dans une zone où les drones se banalisent, ce type de configuration trouve tout son intérêt – même si le golfe de Guinée n’est pas reconnu pour être une zone très chaude en matière de drones kamikazes, contrairement au Moyen-Orient ou bien au théâtre ukrainien.
Au-delà des trois PHA de la Marine nationale, le Rampart pourrait aussi être étendu à d’autres navires d’importance, comme des frégates de premier rang, particulièrement exposés, mais aussi des navires très stratégiques, tels le porte-avions Charles de Gaulle et son successeur (le France Libre, qui accueillera aussi des systèmes laser).

articles.title: Rogue external MFA providers can steal passwords during logins
articles.text:
Security researchers developed an attack that lets hackers with privileged access register a rogue external MFA provider that steals users' passwords during legitimate login attempts.
The technique, dubbed TrustSink by Varonis Threat Labs, can work with any provider that relies on this external authentication model, though the researchers demonstrated the attack using Microsoft Entra.
Microsoft Entra supports external MFA providers, which allow organizations to use third-party authentication services to satisfy multifactor authentication requests.
According to Microsoft, when a user signs in with a first factor, such as a password, Entra can redirect them to an external MFA provider to complete the required second factor.
If the provider returns a valid signed token indicating that the second factor was completed, Entra considers the MFA requirement satisfied.
Varonis found that an attacker who has already compromised a highly privileged Entra account can register a rogue External Authentication Method (EAM) as one of these external MFA providers and use it to insert a convincing Microsoft password prompt into the legitimate authentication flow.
The fake prompt captures the user's password in plaintext before the malicious provider returns a valid signed token to Entra, causing the login to complete without displaying an error.
"In our test tenant, every sign-in completed normally while our server received passwords with timestamps and source IP addresses," explains Varonis.
"Resetting a captured password did not remove the rogue provider. It remained in the authentication flow and captured the replacement password at the user's next sign-in."
It is important to note that TrustSink is not an initial-access attack and requires an attacker to already control a highly privileged Entra account.
Abusing an external MFA provider
TrustSink abuses the trust Microsoft places in a configured external MFA provider.
Varonis created a malicious provider that appeared to Entra as a legitimate external MFA provider but displayed a copy of Microsoft's password page to the user.
During the proof-of-concept attack, the login initially proceeds normally, with the user entering their email address and password on Microsoft's legitimate login.microsoftonline.com site.
When MFA is triggered, Entra redirects the browser to the attacker's external MFA provider for the second authentication step.
Instead of presenting a legitimate second-factor challenge, the malicious provider displays a copy of Microsoft's password prompt.
If the victim enters their password again, believing Microsoft is requesting it as part of the authentication process, the credential is sent to the attacker-controlled server.
The rogue provider then generates a signed token stating the MFA prompt was completed and returns it to Entra, allowing the user to continue to the application they originally attempted to access.
From the victim's perspective, the sign-in appears to have completed normally.
Varonis says the attack is convincing because the fake password prompt appears when the user already expects another authentication step.
The researchers say the page uses the same fonts, layout, and button design as Microsoft's legitimate login page and appears immediately after the victim enters their real password on Microsoft's domain.
Varonis says TrustSink builds on previous research by security researcher Dirk-Jan Mollema, presented at x33fcon 2025 in a talk titled "Bringing Your Own Identity in Entra ID."
Mollema showed how a rogue registered external MFA provider could satisfy an MFA requirement by returning a signed JWT claiming authentication had succeeded without actually performing the expected authentication check.
TrustSink abuses the same attack for credential theft.
Varonis says registering the malicious external method requires modifying the Authentication Methods Policy and creating an application, service principal, and consent grant.
Those actions require a Global Administrator or Authentication Policy Administrator account, making TrustSink a post-compromise technique.
Once installed, however, the rogue provider can remain in the authentication path for targeted users across subsequent logins.
Because the rogue MFA provider remains registered in the tenant's Authentication Methods Policy, even if a user changes their password, it will be recaptured on the next log in attempt.
Varonis therefore warns administrators to remove the malicious provider before rotating affected credentials.
Varonis recommends removing suspicious external MFA providers and their associated applications, keys, and redirect URIs before resetting affected users' passwords.
Organizations should also monitor changes to the Authentication Methods Policy, limit standing Global Administrator and Authentication Policy Administrator privileges, and use phishing-resistant authentication methods such as FIDO2 or Windows Hello for Business.

articles.title: Google Open-Sources AX a Kubernetes Style Orchestrator for Autonomous AI Agents
articles.text:
Google has introduced AX (hosted at agentexecutor.io and on GitHub as google/ax), an open-source, Apache 2.0-licensed orchestrator and declarative runtime designed to execute and scale autonomous AI agent workloads. Running on top of Agent Substrate, AX treats agents as stateful actors rather than microservices or batch jobs, offering sub-second task suspension and resumption alongside four core declarative primitives: Task, Workspace, Gateway, and Model.
Modern AI agents present operational requirements that diverge significantly from traditional infrastructure models. Unlike stateless microservices that handle short-lived request-response lifecycles or batch jobs that execute deterministically to completion, autonomous agents are stateful, bursty, and long-running. They execute intensive compute during reasoning, tool execution, and local code evaluation, interspersed with prolonged idle periods while awaiting model responses, external API feedback, or human-in-the-loop intervention. In conventional Kubernetes or container orchestration setups, keeping dedicated sandboxes active during these idle phases leads to compute underutilization, while cold starts in conventional container runtimes introduce latency that degrades interactive agent loops.
AX addresses this operational profile through an architecture rooted in systems research from teams across Google and Google DeepMind. The platform operates on Agent Substrate, an execution runtime engineered specifically for dense actor multiplexing. In AX, each agent session runs as an isolated actor sandbox with strict CPU and memory resource boundaries. When an agent enters an idle state—such as waiting for an inference provider or a tool call—the platform checkpoints its execution state and suspends it. AX is designed to resume suspended actors in sub-second intervals with zero cold-start delay, multiplexing dozens of tasks onto shared host workers to conserve compute resources.
Image source: Generated with Gemini based on content available on the GitHub project and website
The control plane exposes four declarative Kubernetes-style primitives defined under the ax.io/v1alpha1 API group. The Task primitive defines the execution lifecycle, sandbox resource constraints, and references to supporting infrastructure. The Workspace primitive handles pre-execution environment assembly; developers can declaratively mount Git repositories, configure Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, install skill bundles, or provide natural-language goals that an initialisation agent executes to bootstrap toolchains and system dependencies prior to task start. The Gateway primitive manages outbound network security policies, restricting sandboxed agents to explicit allowlists of hostnames and network ports while handling credential injection into outbound requests. The Model primitive establishes a unified control point for LLM provider parameters, runtime configurations, and secrets stored in Kubernetes.
Image source: Generated with Gemini based on content available on the GitHub project and website
Interaction with the system is driven through the ax command-line tool, written in Go. Platform operators deploy the control plane to Kubernetes using ko and Redis into the ax-system namespace, interfacing through existing Kubernetes contexts via kubectx. Developers manage workloads using commands including ax apply to register manifests, ax watch to stream task phase and condition changes in real time, ax ssh to access interactive sandbox environments for debugging, and ax suspend and ax resume to manually control task execution state. The project is positioned for production agent deployment as well as research environments that require running sandboxed trajectories, reinforcement learning loops, and agent benchmark evaluations at scale.
However, as active discussions on Hacker News demonstrate, the technical community is divided between infrastructure engineers who praise the platform for solving the prohibitive cloud costs of idle agents waiting on model APIs or human input, and developers who criticise the marketing claim of "ergonomic workflows" due to the heavy operational overhead of maintaining Kubernetes clusters, container registries, and custom CRDs via tools like ko. Meanwhile, discussions cross-posted to Reddit emphasise that AX serves as a foundational execution runtime rather than a high-level application orchestrator like LangGraph or CrewAI, while practitioners across security and systems channels highlight the vital blast-radius containment of gVisor-isolated sandboxes alongside early teething issues like egress proxy dropped connections and rudimentary secrets management, ultimately positioning AX not as a quick-start framework for solo hackers, but as an essential compute primitive for enterprises managing large-scale, long-running agentic fleets.

articles.title: Bitcoin: cuál es el precio de esta criptomoneda este día
articles.text:
El bitcoin, la primera moneda virtual lanzada al mercado, fue creado por Satoshi Nakamoto (pseudónimo) en 2008 tras la crisis financiera que afectó al mundo; esta divisa digital tenía como base un ideal libertario y buscaba poner en jaque a las instituciones monetarias y financieras tradicionales.
Conocido en el mundo de los mercados bajo las siglas BTC, el bitcoin utiliza la criptografía para garantizar que su gestión sea descentralizada, es decir, que no pueda ser regulado por ninguna institución u organismo bancario, lo que a su vez hace que las criptomonedas sean volátiles.
PUBLICIDAD
A pesar del avance y alcance que ha tenido el Bitcoin y otros activos digitales de gran talla como Ethereum, organismos como el Banco Mundial, el Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI) y el Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo (BID) aún se muestran dudosos sobre los "pros" de este tipo de criptomonedas.
La victoria electoral de Donald Trump significó un movimiento positivo para las principales criptomonedas del mercado. A finales de 2024, bitcoin registró un nuevo máximo histórico que logró superar los 107.000 dólares por unidad, después de que el presidente estadounidense reiteró su idea de crear una reserva estratégica de la criptodivisa en Estados Unidos.
PUBLICIDAD
Las divisas digitales serán un foco de atención durante este año, las iniciativas del presidente de Estados Unidos y el desarrollo de nuevos modelos de inteligencia artificial fungirán un papel importante en la cotización de estos activos. Después del lanzamiento del nuevo modelo de IA chino DeepSeek, BTC y otras criptos cayeron en la mayoría de los mercados de valores.
Cotización de la criptomoneda Bitcoin
El valor de la criptomoneda de bitcoin para este día a las 14:00 horas (UTC) es de 86003.93 dólares por unidad.
Esto quiere decir que el activo digital mostró un cambio del 0.81% en las últimas 24 horas, así como una variación del 0.0% en la última hora.
PUBLICIDAD
Actualmente, bitcoin se encuentra en el lugar #1 de popularidad en el mercado digital. Cabe mencionar que el máximo histórico que ha alcanzado esta moneda digital es de 126.198 dólares por unidad.
Bitcoin alcanzó su máximo histórico
En marzo del año pasado el bitcoin ha logrado un nuevo máximo histórico, superando los valores anteriores y reafirmándose como la criptomoneda más importante en el mercado, acercándose a los 73 mil dólares. Este récord se obtuvo en medio de un flujo sin precedentes de inversiones hacia las criptomonedas, un acontecimiento notable para el sector financiero digital.
El aumento en el valor de bitcoin ocurre en un contexto donde hay un entrante masivo de capital hacia las criptomonedas, lo que indica un creciente interés y confianza de los inversores en estos activos. La subida del precio beneficia no solo a bitcoin sino que también tiene un impacto positivo en el mercado de las criptomonedas en general, favoreciendo una mayor estabilidad y visibilidad, de acuerdo a un análisis de Bloomberg.
PUBLICIDAD
Expertos financiaron este aumento a diferentes factores, como la adopción institucional de las criptomonedas, la búsqueda de alternativas de inversión debido a la incertidumbre económica mundial y la innovación continua en la tecnología blockchain que respalda a bitcoin y otras divisas digitales. Esta combinación de factores ha creado un entorno propicio para el crecimiento continuo en el valor de Bitcoin.
Cómo adquirir criptomonedas
Para comprarlas e intercambiarlas se utilizan portales especializados. Su valor varía en función de la oferta, de la demanda y del compromiso de los usuarios, por lo que puede cambiar más rápido que el dinero tradicional, pero mientras más gente esté interesada y quiera comprar determinada divisa, mayor será su valor.
PUBLICIDAD
No obstante, quien invierte en este tipo de monedas digitales debe tener muy claro que esta forma trae consigo un elevado riesgo al capital, pues, así como puede haber un incremento, también puede tener inesperadamente un desplome y acabar con los ahorros de sus usuarios.
Para almacenarlas, los usuarios deben contar con un monedero digital o wallet, que en realidad es un software a través del cual es posible guardar, enviar y hacer transacciones de las criptomonedas. En realidad, este tipo de monederos sólo guarda las claves que marcan la propiedad y el derecho de una persona sobre cierta criptomoneda, por lo que estos códigos son los que en realidad se deben proteger.
