articles.title: Nothing to spin off CMF as majority Indian-owned company
articles.text:
Nothing to spin off CMF as majority Indian-owned company
Nothing plans to turn CMF into a standalone Indian company, shifting beyond local manufacturing towards product engineering, R&D and intellectual property development.
Carl Pei’s British consumer electronics company Nothing is moving to separate CMF into a standalone Indian company, with the stated aim of doing more than assembling phones in the country.
Nothing co-founder and chief executive officer Pei said CMF will be majority Indian-owned, headquartered in India and supported by its own local team and research and development operations. Nothing will remain a shareholder and partner.
CMF is Nothing’s sub-brand, launched in 2023 to make design-focused consumer technology more accessible at lower price points.
The significance lies in where value is created. India already makes a significant number of the mobile handsets sold domestically, but local assembly does not necessarily mean that the underlying technology, design or intellectual property is developed in India.
Government data published in April put domestic value addition in electronics manufacturing at 18-20%.
In his article, India Is Inevitable, Pei explained that the next phase of the country’s electronics industry has to move from manufacturing towards product engineering and intellectual property.
“Real R&D is the ability to design, engineer and keep improving a product in-house. It’s what separates a company that lasts from one that rides a moment,” Pei wrote.
By R&D, he means controlling areas such as product structure, thermal performance, cameras, software, antennas and key components, instead of relying mainly on a manufacturing partner.
The proposed CMF structure builds on a manufacturing joint venture announced in 2025 between Nothing and Indian electronics manufacturer Optiemus. The latest arrangement takes the relationship further by bringing manufacturing, ownership and R&D together. Optiemus has said it will initially acquire 51.1% of the proposed joint venture, subject to definitive agreements and other conditions.
The companies noted the expanded partnership will build what they describe as full-stack, end-to-end smartphone R&D in India, covering industrial design, mechanical engineering, camera engineering, software, connectivity and component engineering.
The wider smartphone market provides a more complicated backdrop. India’s smartphone market was broadly flat in 2025, according to Counterpoint data, while shipments fell 10% year-on-year in the June quarter of 2026, the biggest decline for that quarter in six years.
At the same time, policy is attempting to push the industry further up the value chain. The government raised the outlay for the Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme from Rs 22,919 crore to Rs 40,000 crore in Budget 2026, while continuing broader incentives for electronics production and exports.
Global manufacturers are also deepening their India presence. Reuters reported this month that Foxconn and Tata Electronics were ramping up production of Apple’s latest iPhone models in India for export markets, underscoring the country’s growing role in global electronics supply chains.
Pei’s ambition goes considerably further. He noted CMF ultimately wants to reach 100 million phones a year, arguing that scale can give a brand enough influence to shape its supplier ecosystem.
“The only way to get there and stay there is to build in India, not ship to India,” Pei wrote.
Nothing introduced CMF as a separate brand within the company, built around products that emphasise colour, materials and finish while retaining the broader company’s design-led approach. CMF initially expanded across audio, wearables and charging products, and later entered smartphones with the CMF Phone 1 in 2024, followed by the CMF Phone 2 Pro. Its current portfolio includes smartphones, wireless earbuds, over-ear headphones, smartwatches, charging products and other accessories.

articles.title: Des jeux PS5 tournent désormais sur Xbox Series X, merci l'émulation
articles.text:
L’émulation a toujours couru derrière les consoles avec une génération de retard, le temps que les machines soient comprises, disséquées et reproduites. La PS4 est désormais bien servie sur PC, mais la PS5 restait un chantier à peine ouvert, avec une poignée de projets balbutiants. L’un d’eux, l’émulateur Kyty, vient de faire un pas de côté aussi inattendu que spectaculaire : un port expérimental le fait fonctionner directement sur Xbox Series X et Series S, où il exécute ses premiers jeux PS5.
Quake II version PS5, sur la machine de Microsoft
La compatibilité se limiterait pour l’instant à une poignée de titres simples, avec des performances très en retrait (le mot « expérimental » est presque flatteur). Le premier jeu montré en fonctionnement est la version PS5 de Quake II, un classique de 1997 remis au goût du jour. Autant dire que personne n’annulera son achat de PS5 cette semaine.
 
Reste la démonstration technique : émuler une console récente revient à traduire un livre pendant qu’on le lit, phrase par phrase, sans jamais ralentir, et l’exercice pardonne peu. Le port profite néanmoins d’un terrain favorable, puisque la PS5 et la Series X partagent des architectures cousines signées AMD (processeur et puce graphique de la même famille), ce qui rend l’exploit un peu moins fou qu’il n’y paraît, mais pas moins intéressant techniquement : l’émulation n’intervient que sur les fonctions spécifiques à la PS5, le reste étant plutôt « traduit » (pensez à Proton sur SteamOS).
L’émulation PlayStation grignote du terrain
Sur PC, l’émulation PS4 a gagné une maturité telle que le jeu en ligne tourne désormais sans passer par les serveurs de Sony. Cet été, des jeux PS5 s’affichaient déjà, laborieusement, sur Steam Deck. La génération en cours n’attend donc plus la suivante pour être décortiquée : les barrières tombent pendant que les consoles sont encore en rayon.
Pour le joueur, rien d’utilisable à court terme : pas de catalogue, pas de stabilité, pas de promesse. Côté constructeurs, en revanche, l’exclusivité, argument commercial numéro un de cette génération, repose sur des murs que des bénévoles s’amusent désormais à escalader en public.

articles.title: Amazon ha bloqueado a Muse, el agente de compras de Meta. Nunca un veto a un solo bot dijo tanto sobre el futuro de todos los demás
articles.text:
El domingo por la noche, en Estados Unidos, Amazon empezó a bloquear a Muse cada vez que alguien lo usaba para comprar en su tienda. En su lugar aparecía un aviso: el acceso de un agente de IA no autorizado viola las condiciones de uso que el cliente aceptó.
Amazon lo justifica explicando que Meta nunca le avisó de que Muse entraría en su tienda, y el agente no se identifica como tal cuando navega... además de que aparentemente, según Amazon, está almacenando las credenciales de los clientes.
Por qué es importante. Meta lanzó Muse el 8 de septiembre: le das acceso a tu correo, tu calendario y tus pagos, y compra y reserva por ti cualquier cosa en Internet. En una semana ya era la app gratuita más descargada en la App Store de Estados Unidos, por delante de ChatGPT, con más de 900.000 descargas. Es el primer agente de consumo que está consiguiendo unas cifras así.
Entre líneas. Es importante el detalle de cómo está redactado el aviso: no dice que Meta esté entrando sin permiso en los servidores de Amazon, dice que se violan las condiciones de uso que firmó el cliente. No es casualidad. En agosto, un tribunal le quitó a Amazon ese argumento técnico en su pleito contra Perplexity: quien accede a Amazon, dijo, es el usuario, no la empresa de IA.
Lo único que le queda a Amazon es el contrato. La letra pequeña.
Sí, pero. Eso no significa que el riesgo de seguridad sea falso. Es real. Esta semana ha salido un fallo en Muse para Mac que exponía las credenciales del usuario a cualquier otra aplicación del ordenador, y Amazon dice que el navegador de Perplexity iniciaba sesión con los datos del cliente sin identificarse. Eso es tan cierto como que le viene de perlas justo ahora.
El otro lado. Shopify mantiene la puerta abierta a Muse con Shop Pay. Walmart tiene las puertas abiertas para los agentes de Gemini y de OpenAI. La diferencia está en el negocio de cada uno: Amazon ingresó más de 68.000 millones de dólares en publicidad en 2025, y ese negocio exige ojos humanos paseando entre productos patrocinados.
Un humano está expuesto a ellos y eso le dio a Amazon todo ese dinero. Pero un agente enviado por un humano no ve anuncios ni compra por impulso ni se deja engatusar: va a lo que le has pedido, compara, y se larga. Los anuncios son invisibles para ellos y su valor es 0. Así que una parte importante del negocio de Amazon (no es un porcentaje muy alto de sus ingresos pero sí de sus beneficios) se difumina si los agentes triunfan. Por eso han querido dar un portazo a Muse como se lo dieron a Comet.
Entre bambalinas. Amazon tampoco es del todo coherente aquí, porque tiene su propio Alexa for Shopping, y otro agente, Buy for Me, que sale a comprar en otras tiendas. Y Meta, la segunda mayor empresa de publicidad del mundo tras Google, cerró el año pasado WhatsApp a ChatGPT y Copilot hasta que la Comisión Europea la obligó a reabrirlo.
Ambos defienden la apertura en casa ajena y el control en la propia.
Y ahora qué. Esto ya lo hemos visto antes. Dos veces, de hecho:
- La primera, con las aerolíneas. Ryanair se pasó años en guerra con las agencias online que rastreaban su web para revender vuelos con recargo, esas que su CEO llamaba "piratas". Llegó a demandar a Booking en Estados Unidos, un jurado le dio la razón en 2024, y un juez tumbó el veredicto poco después. Lo curioso es cómo acabó todo: en acuerdos comerciales. Ryanair terminó pactando con varias de esas mismas agencias.
- La segunda, con la banca. Hace diez años, las apps que agregaban tus cuentas hacían lo mismo que hace Muse hoy: entraban con tu usuario y tu contraseña y actuaban como si fueran tú. Europa lo resolvió con la PSD2: identifícate, y si estás autorizado, te tengo que dejar pasar.
Ahí está la pista de por dónde puede ir esto. Amazon está pidiendo la primera mitad de esa fórmula. Pero la segunda, de momento, no la promete.
¿Cómo acabará esto? En Estados Unidos, como acaban allí estas cosas: con acuerdos entre gigantes. En Europa, probablemente a golpe de competencia. Lo que no va a cambiar es quién paga, al final, la cuenta del agente que compra por ti: la publicidad.

articles.title: Motorola dévoile le Signature 27, son nouveau smartphone haut de gamme équipé du Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6
articles.text:
C’est un look qui promet de diviser, mais tant pis. Profitant du Snapdragon Summit, où Qualcomm a dévoilé sa toute dernière puce mobile, Motorola a officialisé l’existence de son Signature 27, son futur téléphone haut de gamme pensé pour aller concurrencer les Galaxy S26, iPhone 18 Pro et autres ténors du secteur.
Histoire de se démarquer, Motorola a évidemment tenté de proposer une fiche technique irréprochable et qui promet, sur le papier, d’envoyer du lourd.
iPhone 18 Pro Max à 199€ ! Obtenez 50€ de remise immédiate avec le code NEW50 et jusqu’à 150€ de bonus reprise. Associez-le à un forfait 250Go à 29,99€/mois pendant un an. Livraison offerte.
Le plein de modules photo
Sans surprise, le téléphone est le premier à embarquer le tout nouveau Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6. Cette puce dispose de deux cœurs cadencés à 5 GHz et six autres cadencés à 4 GHz. Un NPU dédié à l’intelligence artificielle promet de faire tourner Gemini et consorts sans problème. Elle est aussi gravée en deux nanomètres, exactement comme la toute nouvelle puce A20 Pro qui trouve sa place dans les iPhone 18 Pro.
Mais là où Motorola veut vraiment se démarquer, c’est sur le côté créatif. Déjà parce que le téléphone a définitivement un design assez original (que ce soit en vert ou en noir) avec son dos en aluminium et sa « surface photographique » qui héberge pas moins de quatre modules photo. Soit un de plus que la plupart des mobiles haut de gamme concurrents.
Le capteur principal de 50 millions de pixels n’est autre qu’un Sony LYT-901 de 1/1,12 pouce (le même que sur l’Oppo Find X9 Ultra), mais surtout un capteur plus grand que celui du Galaxy S27. Un module périscopique de 200 Mpx promet d’offrir un « 100x super Zoom » pour « capturer des détails au loin, l’architecture et les paysages ». Motorola est resté coi sur les deux autres modules, mais on s’attend à ce qu’un capteur ultra grand-angle de 50 Mpx soit de la partie.
Pas encore de prix ou de date de sortie
L’autre caractéristique que la marque veut mettre en avant est son partenariat avec Bang & Olufsen, qui a droit à son petit logo au dos du smartphone. Le téléphone intégrera ainsi des haut-parleurs calibrés directement par les ingénieurs de la marque, plusieurs profils sonores dédiés pour « une expérience sonore pensée pour être ressentie pas juste entendue », quoi que cela veuille dire.
Enfin, Motorola promet sept ans de mises à jour, comme Samsung et Google. C’est d’ailleurs sur cet aspect que l’entreprise devra faire ses preuves. Les composants haut de gamme et les partenariats prestigieux ne font pas forcément un bon téléphone si le logiciel ne suit pas.
    Pour aller plus loin
            GrapheneOS va faire ses débuts sur des téléphones pliables Motorola l’année prochaine
            
La sortie du Signature 27 est prévue pour 2026 sans plus de précisions et Motorola n’a pas encore annoncé de prix.

articles.title: GitLab Duo Expands Self-Hosted AI Options Through Microsoft Foundry
articles.text:
GitLab has expanded GitLab Duo Self-Hosted to support models deployed through Microsoft Foundry, allowing organizations to run GitLab's AI development capabilities against models hosted within their own chosen Azure environment. The integration supports model families including OpenAI GPT, Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, and Mistral, giving enterprises more choice over model provider, deployment location, and data path.
The move is particularly relevant for organizations with data residency, sovereignty, regulatory, or network isolation requirements. Rather than sending AI requests to GitLab-managed model infrastructure, GitLab Duo Self-Hosted can use an organization's own AI Gateway and model deployments. This allows administrators to retain greater control over where requests and responses are processed and how the underlying models are deployed.
The architecture consists of three main components: a self-managed GitLab instance, a self-hosted GitLab AI Gateway, and one or more model endpoints hosted through Microsoft Foundry. The gateway acts as the intermediary between GitLab Duo and the selected models, rather than tying individual Duo features directly to a particular model provider.
An important aspect of the integration is feature-level model selection. Organizations can use different models for different GitLab Duo capabilities - for example, a code-focused model for Code Suggestions, another model for agentic workloads, and a smaller model for higher-volume tasks. Model deployments can also be changed without fundamentally changing the GitLab development workflow.
The approach also highlights an important trade-off with self-hosted AI. Giving organizations control over models and infrastructure provides greater flexibility, but it shifts more responsibility onto engineering and platform teams. They must manage model deployments, capacity, networking, credentials, availability, and model lifecycle in addition to the GitLab environment itself.
It also means that model availability does not automatically equal GitLab Duo compatibility. Microsoft Foundry's catalogue can change faster than GitLab's supported-model matrix, so organizations need to verify compatibility across both platforms before selecting a model.
GitLab's approach follows a broader movement away from treating AI development tools and foundation models as a single bundled service. Microsoft Foundry itself provides access to models from multiple vendors, while GitLab provides the development and DevSecOps layer around them.
There are similarities with other enterprise development platforms. GitHub Copilot, for example, increasingly supports multiple underlying models, but its standard experience remains closely integrated with GitHub's managed service. GitLab's self-hosted model approach instead puts greater emphasis on controlling the AI infrastructure and network path. Meanwhile, platforms such as Amazon Bedrock and Microsoft Foundry itself provide multi-model infrastructure but are not themselves substitutes for an integrated DevSecOps platform such as GitLab.
This makes the development environment increasingly resemble a model-agnostic control layer: GitLab manages the developer workflow and AI features, while the organization can determine which models sit underneath them.
The significance of the announcement therefore extends beyond another model integration. As AI becomes embedded deeper into software engineering, enterprises increasingly need to make decisions not just about which AI capabilities developers use, but where the models run, where source code and prompts travel, who controls the credentials, and which jurisdictions process the data.
GitLab's Microsoft Foundry integration addresses part of that problem by allowing the AI model layer to sit within an organization's chosen Azure environment. Enterprise AI tooling is increasingly moving toward model choice, deployment control, and data sovereignty, rather than assuming that the best development experience requires a single centrally managed AI provider.

articles.title: Tom Cruise alerte sur l'arrivée de l'IA à Hollywood : “Rien ne vaut l'humain”
articles.text:
Tom Cruise alerte sur l'arrivée de l'IA à Hollywood : “Rien ne vaut l'humain”
L'acteur de Mission: Impossible et Top Gun: Maverick a partagé son avis sur l'arrivée de l'intelligence artificielle dans le cinéma, tout en réaffirmant sa foi dans la création humaine.
À l'occasion d'une soirée BAFTA : Life in Pictures qui se déroulait ce lundi, Tom Cruise a réagi à l'incontournable question sur l'intelligence artificielle, et son utilisation au sein d'Hollywood. Et l'acteur de 64 ans, actuellement promo pour son prochain film Digger, a tenu une ligne nuancée, entre lucidité et discours sur la puissance de l'humanité.
"Les gens veulent voir de vraies choses"
Interrogé hier soir par la modératrice Edith Bowman sur l'impact de l'IA sur l'industrie cinématographique, Tom Cruise n'a pas mâché ses mots sur l'usage de l'intelligence artificielle : "vous le savez, c'est en chemin, et c'est en train d'arriver. Mais les gens veulent voir de vraies choses".
La star, qui a récemment affronté une IA maléfique dans le dernier volet de la saga Mission: Impossible, The Final Reckoning, a poursuivi son discours en invitant les réalisateurs à continuer à créer face à l'IA, car "rien ne vaut l'humain".
Au final, Cruise a tenu un long monologue de six minutes dans lequel il a réaffirmé sa foi dans la création humaine, et dans l'expérience de voir un film dans une salle de cinéma : "Je n'ai rien contre le streaming ou quoi que ce soit de ce genre, mais voir un film en salle relève d'une forme d'art différente. Les gens veulent vivre cette expérience, ils vont au cinéma".
Et il faut dire que l'acteur n'a pas tout à fait tort, alors que le cinéma américain a enregistré cet année un record de recettes estivales au box-office, notamment grâce aux cartons de L'Odyssée, Spider-Man : Brand New Day, Obsession et Backrooms.
À l'heure où l'intelligence artificielle a plus que jamais fait son nid dans les usages des studios et dans les processus de production, de nombreuses forces vives de l'industrie ont pris la parole pour un usage plus moral de cette nouvelle technologie.
Alors que Tom Cruise a lui-même était victime de vidéos en deepfake sur YouTube, que Darren Aronofsky a créé une série en IA sur Youtube et Christopher Nolan invite la nouvelle génération à rejeter cette technologie, le débat autour de l'intelligence artificielle est plus que jamais bouillant.
En attendant, les spectateurs pourront retrouver l'acteur dans le nouveau film Digger d'Alejandro González Iñárritu, en salles le 30 septembre prochain.

articles.title: Activision says the Call of Duty cheat economy is now a $8.5 billion industry
articles.text:
In context: Ahead of the much-awaited Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launch on October 22, Activision has published a detailed report on how the global video game cheat economy has evolved into a multi-billion-dollar business spanning subscription services, cheat reskins, illicit accounts, and spoofing hardware, supported by an organized network of hackers, resellers, and distributors.
The company also cited a recent study by threat intelligence firm Intorqa, which claims the cheat economy generates between $5.1 billion and $13.8 billion every year, with the median estimate being around $8.5 billion. The study claims that the cheat economy is made up of two revenue streams: subscription software and a wide network of supporting tools and services.
According to the research data, cheat subscriptions for just 15 popular titles generate around $3.5 billion per year, while account trading, boosting services, hardware ID spoofers, and other tools that are largely sold through organized distributor networks account for at least another $5 billion.
As part of its anti-cheat operations in collaboration with federal and local law enforcement agencies, Activision has reportedly disrupted 375 reseller operations, issued more than 80 cease-and-desist notices, and shut down 31 primary cheat vendors.
The company also recently released a video showing bodycam footage of an alleged Call of Duty cheat maker being served a cease-and-desist order at their Ohio residence.
 – Call of Duty (@CallofDuty) August 28, 2026
Due to the complexity, time, and cost involved in detecting and eliminating cheating in online multiplayer games, Activision says that its Ricochet Anti-Cheat technology does not try to catch one cheater at a time. Instead, it combines "detection, account security, TPM 2.0 enforcement, deep investigations, and legal action" to combat the cheating ecosystem.
The company added that it has adopted a multi-layered approach to counter cheating, whereby each layer targets one of the three pillars of the market: software- and hardware-based cheats, replacement accounts, and evasion tools such as spoofers. Activision is also working with law enforcement to dismantle distribution networks and catch the people operating them.
Explaining the scale and scope of the modern cheating economy, Activision noted that cheating tools include aimbots, wallhacks, rage cheats, unlock tools, DMA-based cheating hardware, and external devices designed to manipulate gameplay, such as Cronus, XIM, and Titan.
Account theft has also become big business, with one out of three gamers reporting that their accounts were hacked within the last two years. According to Activision, the ongoing bans on cheating accounts have created a massive demand for stolen accounts, aged accounts, Ranked Play-ready accounts, and boosting services.
Hardware-based spoofers, evasion tools, and related services are also being sold as part of a thriving online ecosystem helping cheaters evade bans. Activision says it is using "behavioral and technical detections" to thwart spoofers, adding that it issued more than 70,000 new hardware bans in August as part of its ongoing fight against this practice.

Despencou: iPhone 17e (512 GB) tem promoção histórica no Magalu
iPhone 17e (512 GB) traz chip A19 de alto desempenho e câmera de 48 MP; celular acessível da Apple atinge o menor preço histórico com desconto de 34% com cupom
O iPhone 17e de 512 GB está saindo por R$ 4.799 no Pix com cupom INFLU300 no Magazine Luiza. O celular acessível da Apple, equipado com o chip A19 e uma câmera principal de 48 MP, alcança o menor preço histórico com desconto de 34% sobre o original de R$ 7.299.
Mesmo sendo o mais “baratinho” da Apple, o iPhone 17e oferece alto desempenho alinhado com os demais modelos da linha 2025, com o chip A19 (o mesmo do iPhone 17) e os 8 GB de RAM sustentando apps pesados e funções do Apple Intelligence. Seu painel Super Retina XDR OLED de 6,1″ possui um brilho de até 1.200 nits e reproduz imagens com cores vibrantes, além de garantir a visibilidade em qualquer ambiente. O vidro Ceramic Shield 2 protege o display contra pancadas e quedas.

articles.title: Disney+ et les pubs pour tous les abonnements, Disney répond officiellement
articles.text:
L’alerte rouge semblait maximale sur le front de la SVOD. Après l’envoi d’un courriel de la part de Disney+, informant ses utilisateurs d’une mise à jour imminente de ses conditions générales d’abonnement, la toile s’est rapidement enflammée.
En cause : une formulation juridique particulièrement ambiguë indiquant que l’ensemble des formules, y compris celles facturées à 10,99 € et 15,99 € par mois, pouvaient désormais inclure du contenu promotionnel et des publicités avant ou après la lecture d’un programme. De quoi provoquer un véritable tollé chez des abonnés payant le prix fort pour échapper à la réclame.
Suite à cela, le géant du streaming a finalement décidé d’éteindre l’incendie en apportant un droit de réponse officiel à nos confrères de Frandroid ce 22 septembre 2026. La firme aux grandes oreilles s’est voulue catégorique : malgré des termes contractuels qui laissaient craindre le pire, aucune publicité traditionnelle ne viendra perturber l’expérience de visionnage des abonnés aux offres Standard et Premium.
Une précision juridique plus qu’une vraie pause commerciale pour Disney+
Afin de clarifier cet imbroglio, la plateforme a tenu à préciser la nature exacte des éléments mentionnés dans ses nouvelles règles. Disney+ explique que le terme « publicité », au sens strictement juridique du contrat, fait référence à des pratiques déjà en vigueur et strictement encadrées par le secteur. Il s’agit principalement d’auto-promotion, comme la diffusion de bandes-annonces pour d’autres séries ou films du catalogue, ainsi que de contenus sponsorisés intégrés aux événements en direct et retransmissions sportives.
En réalité, la formule « Standard avec pub » reste à ce jour la seule et unique offre soumise aux coupures publicitaires régulières pendant le visionnage d’une œuvre. Si les conditions générales laissent techniquement la porte ouverte à des messages promotionnels aux bornes des vidéos, Disney+ promet de maintenir son engagement contractuel en garantissant un confort de visionnage total pour ses offres supérieures. De quoi rassurer les usagers, même si cette maladresse de communication aura provoqué une belle frayeur chez les abonnés.
La tentation de la publicité dans le streaming payant
Bien que cet incident se termine par une mise au point apaisante, l’émoi suscité par l’affaire témoigne de la nervosité ambiante des consommateurs face aux services de SVOD. Dans une industrie en quête constante de rentabilité, la frontière entre formules financées par les annonceurs et abonnements « purement » payants a tendance à devenir de plus en plus floue chez certains concurrents. La moindre modification des CGU est désormais scrutée avec une méfiance compréhensible par les utilisateurs, échaudés par les hausses de tarifs répétées et le blocage du partage de compte.
En clarifiant sa position auprès de la presse spécialisée, Disney+ évite pour l’instant une vague de résiliations massives. La balle reste désormais dans le camp du géant américain, qui devra prouver dans les faits et sur la durée que la promesse d’une expérience fluide sans interruption commerciale sera bien tenue.

articles.title: Cable Matters Introduces 40 Gbps USB4 KVM Switch for Two Laptops
articles.text:
Tuesday, September 22nd 2026
	
	
	
	
Cable Matters Introduces 40 Gbps USB4 KVM Switch for Two Laptops
Cable Matters introduces its 40 Gbps USB4 KVM Switch for two laptops, model 201342, designed to simplify workspaces shared by two computers. Users can switch a compatible USB-C monitor or docking station between laptops, giving the selected computer access to the connected display and peripherals without repeatedly moving cables.
Jeff Jiang, President of Cable Matters Inc."Switching between a work laptop and a personal computer should be simple. The new USB4 KVM switch lets users share a compatible monitor or docking station at the press of a button, making it easier to use both computers in one organized workspace."
The switch combines two built-in host cables and one built-in output cable in a compact enclosure. Users can select a computer with the onboard button or included RF remote control, which operates without a direct line of sight.
Rated capabilities include data rates up to 40 Gbps, video output up to 8K at 60 Hz, 6K at 60 Hz, or 4K at 240 Hz, and USB Power Delivery pass-through up to 140 W. Actual performance depends on the connected computer, monitor or dock, and other equipment. Charging power passes to the selected laptop only and depends on the power source and receiving computer.
Compatible with Thunderbolt 4 and Thunderbolt 5 equipment, the switch supports connections up to its 40 Gbps limit. A compatible docking station or monitor allows users to share its connected keyboard, mouse, storage, and other peripherals between computers, helping reduce duplicate equipment on the desk.
Compatible docking stations must have a detachable host cable. Docks with permanently attached host cables cannot be connected using a USB-C coupler, and USB-C extension cables are not supported. Video output requires a compatible host port with display support; a USB-C data-only port cannot provide video. Supported resolutions, refresh rates, and display configurations depend on the host computer and connected equipment.

I find it easier to just use a single device that acts like both a KVM and a dock at once.
I still think this is a bit on the more expensive side given that it's just a KVM switch without anything else, but it's not as bad as I had thought.
On top of that, it can handle 140 W USB-PD power, something I haven't seen any similar device being capable of.

articles.title: Microsoft estaría preparando nueva ola de despidos en Xbox y la reorganización de estudios de videojuegos
articles.text:
Xbox podría recortar cientos de puestos de trabajo y reorganizar parte de sus estudios de videojuegos, según The Information. La eventual medida formaría parte de una nueva etapa de reestructuración de Microsoft, aunque la compañía no ha confirmado públicamente los cambios.
La posible reorganización se sumaría a un plan de despidos que, según el medio mencionado, contemplaría 3.200 puestos de trabajo en Xbox antes de junio de 2027.
PUBLICIDAD
Los antecedentes de la reestructuración de Xbox
En julio, Microsoft despidió a 4.800 empleados en una nueva ronda de recortes orientada a reducir costos y redirigir recursos hacia la inteligencia artificial.
La compañía buscaba mejorar su eficiencia mientras enfrentaba la presión de rentabilizar sus inversiones en inteligencia artificial, cuyos gastos también elevaron los costos de infraestructura y hardware.
En Xbox, Asha Sharma reconoció que el negocio atraviesa dificultades financieras: Game Pass no habría crecido al ritmo esperado, el margen de beneficio cayó al 3% y los ingresos anuales disminuyeron en casi USD 500 millones pese a inversiones superiores a USD 20.000 millones.
En su momento, se prevía que la reestructuración también alcanzaría a cuatro estudios. Compulsion Games y Double Fine Productions volverían a operar de forma independiente, manteniendo sus derechos de propiedad intelectual y recursos para futuros proyectos.
PUBLICIDAD
Ninja Theory y Undead Labs pasarían a nuevos propietarios que aportarían financiación para continuar con el desarrollo de Senua y State of Decay 3. En Francia, Arkane se encontraría en un proceso de consulta para definir opciones estratégicas.
Xbox impondrá límites de tiempo al mes para usar Cloud gaming
Xbox impondrá desde noviembre de 2026 límites mensuales de juego en la nube para los suscriptores de Game Pass Ultimate, Premium y Essential. El cambio reemplazará el acceso sin tope de horas que hasta ahora tenían los usuarios elegibles y, según la compañía, alcanzará al 4% de los suscriptores.
Game Pass Ultimate incluirá 15 horas mensuales de juego en la nube; Premium, 10 horas, y Essential, cinco. Una vez consumido ese tiempo, los jugadores podrán adquirir horas adicionales en la Xbox Store.
PUBLICIDAD
La empresa adelantó que los precios, los juegos compatibles, la disponibilidad y las opciones de compra variarán según el mercado y se anunciarán antes de la entrada en vigor de la medida.
Xbox también permitirá comprar horas de juego en la nube sin contar con una suscripción a Game Pass. Esta alternativa estará dirigida a quienes quieran transmitir ocasionalmente títulos elegibles que ya posean desde dispositivos compatibles.
La función también permitirá a los propietarios de Xbox One acceder a determinados juegos desarrollados para Xbox Series X|S sin actualizar su consola.
La compañía sostuvo que los límites buscan sostener el servicio e invertir en su rendimiento y fiabilidad, ante el aumento de los costos operativos a medida que crece el uso del juego en la nube.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo van las ventas de Xbox en 2026
Las ventas de consolas Xbox en Estados Unidos registraron en mayo de 2026 su peor resultado histórico para ese mes, según un hilo publicado por el analista Matt Piscatella en BlueSky.
Las unidades de hardware de la marca alcanzaron el nivel más bajo desde el inicio de estas mediciones, en 1995.
El mercado estadounidense habría estado liderado durante mayo y en el acumulado de 2026 por Nintendo Switch 2, seguida por PlayStation, mientras Xbox quedó en último lugar. La caída de las ventas físicas es vinculada con el encarecimiento de las consolas, la escasez de componentes y el aumento de los costos de memoria y almacenamiento interno.
PUBLICIDAD
Xbox anunciara un incremento global de precios para las Series X|S. De acuerdo con LA compañía, los modelos de 512 GB subirían USD 100 y los de 1 TB, USD 150. Además, la compañía dejaría de fabricar la versión de 2 TB.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (September 22, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (September 22, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Tuesday, September 22, 2026.
Indian women’s cricket team brought in the first gold medal for the country at the ongoing Asian Games 2026 as companies line up to go public, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Featured news
Deoria MP Shashank Mani Tripathi on the 2026 NEET crisis, India's growth story and entrepreneurship
A paper leak, a resignation and a rocket launch, how one MP connects examinations, growth and enterprise into a single argument.
Meet the solar didis turning sunlight into a source of livelihood in rural Bihar
In Bihar’s Muzaffarpur district, solar didis use clean energy to bring water to farms, build incomes, and gain financial independence.
Today’s key developments
Women's cricket team gives India first gold of 2026 Asian Games
The Indian women's cricket team reasserted its continental dominance by clinching a second successive gold medal at the Asian Games, thrashing familiar foes Sri Lanka by 147 runs on Tuesday. The Harmanpreet Kaur-led side's gold was India's first of the ongoing edition and was shaped by a brilliant batting performance that left Sri Lanka chasing a record target of 217.
Snapdeal parent firm AceVector's IPO to open on September 25
AceVector plans to raise Rs 420 crore through the IPO and has priced its shares in the range of Rs 30-32.
Spinny files confidential IPO papers, eyes upto Rs 3,000 Cr
In August, Spinny’s parent company Valuedrive Technologies converted from a private limited company into a public limited company.
Captain Fresh revenue crosses Rs 5,000 Cr in FY26; co targets Rs 10,000 Cr in FY27
The packaged seafood company saw adjusted EBITDA rise by 173% in FY26 as it remained net profit positive for the second consecutive year.
Funding news
Definedge raises Rs 22 crore in Pre-Series A round
Pune-based fintech and brokerage firm Definedge Securities Broking has raised Rs 22 crore in a Pre-Series A funding round, taking its total capital raised to Rs 30 crore. The round saw participation from existing investors Nitin Agarwal and D Prasad, along with new investors Anant Jain and Sachin Kasera. The company plans to deploy the funds towards infrastructure, low-latency execution, product development, marketing and distribution, and AI and automation capabilities.
Definedge is targeting Rs 5,000 crore in assets under management through its Momentify platform over the next 24 months, having already crossed ₹1,000 crore. It will also expand Algostra, its no-code retail algorithmic trading platform, and scale its investor education ecosystem, Gurukul. The company said its overall user base has grown 125% in 14 months.
Protein Pantry raises Rs 9 cr led by Sharrp Ventures
Protein Pantry, a high-protein frozen food brand has raised Rs 9 crore in a seed round funding. The round was led by Sharrp Ventures, with participation from Peercheque, Consumer Collective by Atrium and Indian Silicon Valley Capital, alongside angels including Varun Alagh (Honasa), Rishubh Satiya (Plix), Avnish Anand (CaratLane), Arush Chopra (Just Herbs), Saurabh Munjal (Lahori Zeera), Signal Ventures and others.
The capital will primarily be deployed into setting up and scaling the brand's manufacturing unit, alongside continued investment in R&D and supply chain. The balance goes into marketing and working capital. Protein Pantry is also extending its ranges with new formats. Over the next 12 to 24 months, the company is targeting availability across all major Indian cities via D2C and quick commerce and continued expansion of its protein range across categories. Since launching in November 2025, Protein Pantry has gone live direct-to-consumer across Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru and Jaipur, and on quick commerce via Blinkit, FirstClub and Flipkart Minutes across Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad.
Demoverse raises $600K led by Lumikai
AI-powered co-creation platform Demoverse has raised $600,000 in a pre-seed funding round led by Lumikai, which invested $500,000 through its Pixels programme. The round also saw participation from UAE-based investor-operator Marlan and angel investors. Demoverse enables consumer brands to involve customers in product creation before production begins. Brands post concepts and design directions, while consumers use AI to reshape and refine them. The community then evaluates and votes on designs, generating product direction and demand signals before manufacturing commitments.
Contributors whose ideas influence winning products can earn royalties when those products are commercialised. The company is initially focusing on fashion and plans to expand into beauty, consumer packaged goods and other categories. Founded by Akshay Mehta, Demoverse has already conducted trials with Indian consumer brands and plans to convert these partnerships into paid campaigns.
YNOS receives Rs 2.12 Cr investment from Gyan Circle Ventures
YNOS, a technology platform providing information and fundraising analytics for India’s startup ecosystem, has received an investment of Rs 2.12 crore from Category-I venture capital fund Gyan Circle Ventures. The funding will support YNOS in expanding its technology capabilities and widening its reach among entrepreneurs and investors. The platform aggregates information on startups, founders, incubators, angel investors, venture capital firms, corporates, government agencies and banks. It provides tools for valuation estimation, investor identification, competition analysis and ecosystem mapping.
As of September 2026, YNOS covers more than 3.42 lakh startups, 5.92 lakh founders, 14,667 angel investors, 6,310 VCs, 1,458 incubators, 137 government schemes and 1,096 banks and financial institutions. More than 875 startups have used YNOS for fundraising, collectively raising around ₹4,000 crore.
TimBuckDo raises bridge round ahead of Series A
Bengaluru-based on-demand convenience platform TimBuckDo has raised a bridge round backed by Srinath Setty, Co-founder and CEO of Hosachiguru, through family office Trasa Ventures, and Adarsh Narahari, Founder and Managing Director of Primus Senior Living. The company has not disclosed the size or valuation of the round. The funding will support technology development, expansion of its verified student workforce, deeper presence in existing markets and expansion of service categories ahead of a planned Series A round.
TimBuckDo operates a network of educated college students, known as “Doers”, who provide flexible, on-demand services including elder companionship, pet care, child support, errands and assistance to home businesses. The company aims to build an organised marketplace connecting verified student talent with households and businesses while enabling students to earn flexibly alongside their education.
Other news
Delvitech to invest up to $30M in Bengaluru facility
Swiss AI-native Automated Optical Inspection company Delvitech has announced plans to establish a manufacturing and technology facility in Bengaluru with an initial investment of $10 million and an overall investment of $25-30 million. The 65,000-square-foot facility is expected to become operational in the first quarter of calendar 2027 and could create 500-800 jobs over the next five years.
The plant will integrate precision machining, metrology and equipment integration, alongside mechanical, electrical, optical, software and control systems. It will also support engineering and R&D activities, product demonstrations and customer trials. Delvitech said the investment reflects its long-term commitment to India’s electronics manufacturing sector. The company showcased its Horus, Aton and Horus Dual Lane inspection solutions at productronica India 2026 in Bengaluru, highlighting AI-driven approaches to electronics quality inspection and manufacturing efficiency.
Simplilearn partners with Karmayogi Bharat for AI skilling
Digital skills training company Simplilearn has partnered with Karmayogi Bharat under the Government of India’s Mission Karmayogi to provide AI and digital upskilling programmes for public sector professionals. The programmes will be hosted on the iGOT Karmayogi platform and cover foundational and advanced topics including artificial intelligence, data analytics, cloud computing, cybersecurity, Generative AI and project management.
The partnership is designed to provide government officials with flexible, self-paced learning that can be integrated into their daily workflows. Karmayogi Bharat said the initiative will help strengthen capabilities across roles and support digitally enabled public administration. Simplilearn said its AI-first learning architecture and SkillUp platform will support continuous learning at scale. The company operates globally across 150-plus countries and offers more than 1,500 live classes each month, reaching over 15 million learners.
Integra Robotics secures Indian patent for remote robotic manipulation
Integra Robotics, a unit of Social Hardware International, has secured Indian Patent No. 597459 for a system enabling remote manipulation of robotic platforms through a virtual reality interface. The patented technology allows human operators to control robots remotely using VR, camera-based depth information and gesture gloves that provide electronic feedback. The architecture integrates VR headsets, motion sensors, infrared gesture gloves, processing modules, network routers and robotic manipulators. Human movements are translated into robotic commands using Bio-Inverse Kinematics.
The technology is designed for applications where direct human intervention may be difficult or hazardous, including industrial operations, inspection, defence and disaster response. Integra Robotics has also filed two additional patent applications covering platform-independent robotic manipulation and operator-intent transformation. The company said the technology strengthens its intellectual property portfolio in advanced robotics and immersive teleoperation.
Masters’ Union Demo Day sees Rs 60 Cr in funding commitments
Masters’ Union Ventures held its first Demo Day in Bengaluru, with 25 student-led startups securing soft-funding commitments of nearly Rs 60 crore within an hour of their pitches. The event brought together more than 65 venture capital firms and angel investors, with participating startups spanning AI, climate and space technology, biotechnology, consumer businesses and advanced manufacturing.
Sanyark, Saubha Aerial Systems and CarbonM were among the startups receiving significant investor interest. The event also featured an AI hackathon conducted with Qualcomm Developer and the launch of a guidebook titled ‘Don’t Start a Stupid Startup’. About 60% of participating startups were built through Masters’ Union’s Venture Initiation Programme. The programme and related initiatives have supported more than 80 student startups, while 50 VIP-incubated ventures have collectively raised over ₹320 crore.
Matters.AI and Cockroach Labs integrate for data security
Bengaluru-based Matters.AI and New York-based Cockroach Labs have announced an integration that identifies personal and regulated data within CockroachDB deployments at the column level and maps it to users, roles and privileges with access. The solution scans databases, tables and columns using 38 personally identifiable information detectors covering eight regulatory jurisdictions, along with payment card data, protected health information and secrets stored in free-text fields.
The system produces a live access map showing which accounts can access regulated data and where data may be stored in inappropriate jurisdictions. Classification and privilege analysis take place inside customers’ infrastructure, while raw records and sampled values are not transmitted. The companies said the integration can support compliance with frameworks including India’s DPDP Act, PCI DSS, HIPAA, GDPR, ISO 27001 and SOC 2.
Stratbeans expands AI-led workforce learning solutions
AI-led enterprise learning company Stratbeans is helping manufacturing organisations improve workforce skills, training coverage and employee performance through digital learning and AI-powered knowledge solutions. Its Ask AI platform enables employees to obtain answers to work-related questions using approved standard operating procedures, policies, manuals and training documents. The company combines digital learning, AI-powered assessments, multilingual learning and intelligent knowledge support. Stratbeans said training coverage at one organisation increased from 20% to 85%, while platform usage reached 80% and the average assessment pass rate stood at 88%.
Its solutions also include Proctored Evaluation for assessments and SIM Studio, which allows employees to practise workplace scenarios through roleplay and receive AI-generated feedback. The company said Ask AI can also help managers identify frequently searched topics and areas where additional training or documentation may be required.
Fynd brings virtual eyewear try-on to Vision Express India
AI-native retail technology company Fynd has partnered with Vision Express India to introduce immersive eyewear shopping through its GlamAR 3D virtual try-on and augmented reality solution. Integrated into the Vision Express website, the technology allows customers to virtually try different eyewear styles. Fynd converted more than 1,000 existing two-dimensional eyewear product assets into production-ready 3D models and brought them live for virtual try-on.
Since launch, the experience has recorded more than 3,900 virtual try-on interactions. Black Square Frames for Men emerged as the most tried-on frame, with more than 400 interactions, while the top 11 frames accounted for nearly 34% of total try-on activity. The next phase will focus on measuring conversions and optimising the online shopping experience using customer try-on behaviour to inform eyewear merchandising.
TalentGum receives STEM.org accreditation and recognition
Online extracurricular learning platform TalentGum has received the STEM.org Accredited Educational Experience Trustmark from STEM.org Educational Research. The company has also been named among the Top 5% of “Best in STEM” brands in a separate recognition. TalentGum said the accreditation provides independent validation of its learning proposition as it expands its extracurricular and skill-based programmes for children. The STEM.org accreditation evaluates educational experiences against a framework focused on interdisciplinary learning and real-world application.
TalentGum offers live courses covering areas including coding, artificial intelligence and machine learning, chess, arts, dance and public speaking. The platform is used by parents across more than 70 countries. The company said the recognition reinforces its focus on helping children develop transferable skills, critical thinking, communication and practical problem-solving through interactive learning experiences.
Atom Risk Advisory secures global insurance broking licence
Atom Risk Advisory, an Indian insurance intermediary operating since 2019, has announced that its group entity has secured a global insurance broking licence. The licence will enable the company to enter international insurance markets and offer cross-border insurance solutions to clients. Atom said its global offering will cover areas including Universal Life Insurance, Private Placement Life Insurance, Keyman Insurance and bespoke legacy solutions. The company plans to strengthen partnerships with international insurers and reinsurers, expand specialist teams and invest in technology-driven risk advisory capabilities.
The move comes as Indian enterprises and family offices expand their international footprint and face increasingly complex risk, wealth and succession planning requirements. Atom Risk Advisory specialises in life and health insurance, family protection, corporate insurance, succession planning and legacy solutions. It is part of Atom Financial Services Group, which also has capabilities in wealth management, investment banking and estate planning.
MyBranch expands South India workspace network
Flexible workspace and managed office provider MyBranch has expanded its South India presence to a 50,000-square-foot footprint across 16 centres in 14 cities spanning Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Telangana.
Its network covers Bengaluru, Coimbatore, Guntur, Hanamkonda, Hubballi, Hyderabad, Madurai, Mangaluru, Rajahmundry, Salem, Tirupati, Vellore, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam, with another large office planned in Chennai. According to JLL data cited by the company, Bengaluru and Hyderabad together accounted for 49.7% of India’s net office absorption in H1 2026, while flexible workspace represented 27% of gross office leasing. MyBranch said its network is designed to support enterprises, MNCs, GCCs, startups and growing businesses establishing regional offices or satellite teams. Founded in 2016, the company now has more than 80 locations across 75-plus cities.
Lxme partners with Shiprocket to expand UPI reach
Financial platform Lxme has partnered with Shiprocket to expand the reach of Lxme UPI across India’s direct-to-consumer commerce ecosystem. The integration is already live across Shiprocket’s Fastrr merchant ecosystem, allowing merchants to offer Lxme UPI without additional integrations. Eligible transactions can also earn customers Digital Gold, linking everyday payments with wealth-building. The partnership is expected to expand Lxme UPI’s availability across hundreds of merchant websites spanning categories such as beauty, grocery and D2C commerce.
Lxme said the initiative supports its strategy of encouraging women to participate in wealth creation through everyday financial transactions. The partnership is non-exclusive, allowing Lxme to continue expanding its merchant network. Shiprocket said the collaboration aims to add greater value to the checkout experience for consumers and D2C brands.
Olyv appoints Ravi Sharma as Chief Financial Officer
Digital lending platform Olyv has appointed Ravi Sharma as its Chief Financial Officer as the company enters its next phase of growth. Sharma brings more than 17 years of experience across financial services and has previously served as CFO at Finova Capital. During his tenure at Finova, he helped lead financial initiatives, close five equity funding rounds and onboard more than 50 lending partners. At Olyv, Sharma will oversee financial strategy, capital planning, risk governance and long-term value creation as the company expands its portfolio of financial products and services.
HCLTech selected by M Group for IT transformation
HCLTech has been selected by UK and Ireland-based essential infrastructure services provider M Group to modernise and transform its IT operations across more than 200 locations. Under the engagement, HCLTech will deploy AI-led managed services covering infrastructure and end-user operations, using its AI Force service transformation platform. The programme will seek to streamline M Group’s IT environment, improve resilience and establish a scalable digital foundation.
The transformation will support M Group’s businesses across water, energy, technology and communications, transport, defence, industrial and public sectors. M Group said the partnership will help strengthen IT reliability and scalability while supporting innovation and sustainable growth. HCLTech said its experience in complex, multi-site environments would support M Group’s technology transformation. HCLTech has more than 223,000 employees across 60 countries, with revenues of $14.8 billion for the 12 months ended June 2026.
Zurich Kotak launches digital insurance proposition for SMEs
Zurich Kotak General Insurance has launched a digital-first insurance proposition aimed at simplifying business protection for small and medium enterprises. Powered by Zurich’s technology platform, Zurich Edge, the solution brings quotation, purchasing, servicing, referrals and underwriting together through a single interface.
Its Business Secure Plus proposition offers bundled protection across areas including fire and special perils, burglary, electronic equipment, fidelity guarantee, directors and officers liability, employee compensation, money and machinery breakdown. Zurich Kotak said the platform enables businesses to obtain customised coverage and premiums based on their risk profiles, with policy issuance possible within minutes. The insurer said SMEs’ contribution to India’s GDP and their employment role underline the need for easier access to insurance. Zurich Kotak is a 70:30 joint venture between Zurich Insurance Group and Kotak Mahindra Bank.
Ubalance Naturals unveils ‘The Forest Within’ brand identity
Ayurvedic wellness company Ubalance Naturals has introduced a new brand identity, ‘The Forest Within’, across its portfolio of nine products and 18 SKUs. The company also announced an ambition to reach ₹100 crore in revenue by FY30. The new identity reflects the company’s philosophy that wellbeing is shaped by interconnected bodily systems rather than isolated functions. Ubalance Naturals said it sees opportunities in India’s growing Ayurvedic wellness market, with industry estimates cited by the company placing the market at around $11.9 billion in 2025 and projecting it to reach $43.2 billion by 2034. The company combines Ayurvedic principles with contemporary scientific understanding and offers formulations addressing areas including energy, stress response, digestive and liver wellness, metabolic health, respiratory wellness and mobility. The new identity will extend across packaging, digital platforms, e-commerce and retail touchpoints.
QNu Labs launches QShield 2.0 for quantum security assessment
Quantum security company QNu Labs has launched QShield 2.0, the platform powering its National Cryptographic Assessment & Assurance Framework, at its 10th anniversary event in Bengaluru. The framework is designed to help organisations identify and assess their cryptographic assets as they prepare for the transition to post-quantum security. QNu Labs said the platform operates through three processes: Discover, Assess and Assure. QShield 2.0 includes modules covering quantum entropy, quantum-readiness risk assessment, quantum PKI, quantum vault and AI security.
The launch comes after a Department of Science and Technology task force report in February 2026 recommended that critical infrastructure sectors begin formal post-quantum cryptography implementation by 2027. The company said early deployment accounts include banks and security depositories. QNu Labs has been incubated at IIT Madras Research Park and has received support from India’s National Quantum Mission.
Apurva.ai expands LENS into cross-organisational knowledge platform
Apurva.ai has announced a new platform model for Apurva LENS, expanding it from an organisation-level knowledge tool into a platform designed to support learning and collaboration across the wider development ecosystem. The AI-enabled platform helps funders, governments, NGOs and change leaders connect research, evaluations, programme experience and community voices. Apurva.ai said LENS has helped surface more than half a million voices and perspectives from the Global South. Under the new model, organisations can share selected knowledge while retaining control over private information.
The platform has been used by organisations including SELCO Foundation and Resilience Action Network Africa to organise and analyse institutional knowledge, community dialogues and research. In Brazil, Museu da Pessoa has used LENS to explore patterns across an archive of life stories. The platform aims to connect fragmented knowledge while retaining local context and human judgement.
Privacy by Design 2026 brings startups and investors together in Bengaluru
DPDP Zone’s Privacy by Design 2026 summit brought together 350 attendees, including 250 founders and 35 investors and fund representatives, in Bengaluru. The event focused on privacy, cybersecurity, responsible AI and digital trust as businesses prepare for India’s Digital Personal Data Protection framework. A separate invite-only Demo Session enabled 15 startups to pitch directly to investors. Participating funds included Bessemer Venture Partners, Kalaari Capital, Blume Ventures, Chiratae Ventures, Inflection Point Ventures, Campus Fund and Venture Catalysts. The programme featured technical sessions and panel discussions covering privacy by design, responsible AI, cybersecurity, founder trust and governance in fundraising. Organisers said the event was held eight weeks before provisions governing Consent Managers under the DPDP Rules were scheduled to take effect on November 13, 2026. Substantive provisions of the Act are scheduled for enforcement from May 13, 2027.
KEDGE launches 18-month MBA programme in India
European business school KEDGE has announced the launch of its MBA programme in India in association with keeplearning. The 18-month programme will combine face-to-face teaching, asynchronous learning and a 14-day in-person immersion, allowing working professionals to pursue the qualification without leaving their careers. Participants will receive an MBA credential directly from KEDGE and access to its alumni network of more than 90,000 graduates. The curriculum covers strategy, finance, marketing, operations, leadership, innovation, international management and sustainable enterprise. It also includes India-focused modules on Generative AI for business operations and responsible AI governance.
The programme features simulations, masterclasses, leadership workshops, coaching and a capstone project based on a live business challenge. The inaugural cohort will be limited, with selection involving an academic assessment, mini-case presentation and interview.
Globe Moving appoints Smartya Majumder as Country Head – Sales
Workforce and workplace mobility company Globe Moving has appointed Smartya Majumder as Country Head – Sales. He brings more than 19 years of experience across logistics and telecom, with previous leadership roles at TNT India, Samsung Electronics, Vivo Mobile India, DHL–Blue Dart Express and DTDC. Before joining Globe Moving, Majumder served as Vice President and National Sales and Marketing Head at Trackon. In his new role, he will oversee sales strategy, revenue growth, business development and customer-focused mobility solutions.

articles.title: This fake LastPass Authenticator app will just shut off your antivirus and leave you open to attack
articles.text:
This fake LastPass Authenticator app will just shut off your antivirus and leave you open to attack
Researchers found a never-before-seen malware targeting LastPass users
- Attackers spoofed LastPass Authenticator via SEO‑poisoned GitHub pages, delivering malicious ZIP files
- Malware Rapuncel uses DLL sideloading, kills 145 AV products, and steals passwords, wallets, and tokens
- Campaign ongoing for months; LastPass vaults unaffected, but users urged to download only from trusted sources
Be careful when downloading the LastPass Authenticator app - there are impostors out there that can disable your antivirus and wreak havoc on your computer.
LastPass recently discovered an elaborate scheme to get people infected with malware - a spoofed website, SEO poisoning, DLL sideloading, and a malware loader delivering never-before-seen payload that can kill endpoint protection and antivirus solutions.
According to the password manager, users searching for "LastPass Authenticator download" or similar keywords will get a GitHub page rather high on the search engine results pages. At a glance, the page looks almost identical to the authentic LastPass offering - however, it redirects users to a separate one, hosted on attacker-controlled infrastructure and delivering a large .ZIP file with multiple files.
Among the files are two worth paying attention to: vsdbg.exe, and vsdbg.dll. The .EXE one is renamed to look like a LastPass installer, but it’s in fact a legitimate Microsoft debugging tool. This tool is used to run the malware - the vsdbg.dll file. This is a method called “dll sideloading” where the legitimate program will look for a DLL file in the same folder it’s located, rather than the wider device library. Since the DLL is delivered together with the executable, it is the first one to be run, despite the fact that it’s malicious.
Rapuncel
LastPass shared the malware with security researchers Delphos for analysis, and they’ve named it Rapuncel. No AV engines have been able to spot it, when it was first analyzed.
Once Rapuncel runs, it does a number of things. First, it gains admin-level access to run as SYSTEM, and then installs a kernel driver. The driver, disguised as an NVIDIA graphics component, comes with a hardcoded list of 145 antivirus and endpoint security products, and if any of them are found on the device, they are instantly terminated.
After killing antivirus solutions, the malware gets to work, stealing saved passwords from more than 25 browsers (Chrome, Edge, and other popular ones included), cryptocurrency wallet files from more than 30 wallet apps, Discord login tokens, Steam session tokens, Telegram session data, Windows credential store, all documents with words like “password”, “seed”, “wallet”, or “recovery” in their name, screenshots of every monitor connected to the device, as well as a detailed profile of the system.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Once all of this is harvested, the information is compressed into a .ZIP archive and uploaded to a server under the attackers’ control. To add insult to injury, the kernel driver was given code to intercept all web traffic, allowing the attackers to inject ads, or modify search results, at a whim.
Rapuncel comes with a persistence mechanism, as well, to make sure it continues operating even if the victim spots it. Spotting it should not be too difficult, though - if no antivirus programs are allowed to run on a computer, something is definitely not working properly.
Active for months
Still, the malware installs itself as a Windows service that starts automatically at boot, and then loops continuously, checking for security products and killing them as soon as they’re activated. “The machine may remain fully under the attacker's control until the kernel driver is physically removed,” the researchers explained. “This process requires booting the computer into Safe Mode or using an external recovery tool, because normal Windows tools cannot safely remove software operating at that level while the system is running.”
LastPass and Delphos believe the campaign has been active for months, and that it will continue to operate despite disruption efforts:
“The LastPass lure was a single recent frame in a campaign that has been running for months and shows every sign of continuing after its current infrastructure is burned,” the researchers said. They stressed that this is “opportunistic brand impersonation” and that LastPass systems and customer vaults have not been compromised or involved in any way.
LastPass said it was one of 40 companies spoofed in this campaign and has urged users to only download apps from reputable, vetted sources.

articles.title: ‘We’ll be the first to mine Bitcoin in space’ says Nvidia-backed startup —Starcloud will fire up its ASICs after its second spacecraft reaches orbit later this year
articles.text:
‘We’ll be the first to mine Bitcoin in space’ says Nvidia-backed startup —Starcloud will fire up its ASICs after its second spacecraft reaches orbit later this year
Almost constant solar energy plus ASIC price per KW are the most compelling aspects of the plan.
An Nvidia-backed startup plans to establish a Bitcoin mining operation in space before the year is out. Starcloud will fire up its cryptocurrency mining ASICs after its second spacecraft reaches orbit later this year. “We’ll be the first to mine Bitcoin in space,” claimed Starcloud CEO Philip Johnston in a recent interview with Documenting Bitcoin.
Starcloud was founded in 2024 with the headlining goal of moving data centers to space. “As launch costs fall, data centers in space will leverage continuous solar energy and radiative cooling, rapidly scaling to gigawatts while avoiding permitting constraints on Earth,” reads its mission statement. The firm spells out its proposition in far greater detail in a white paper on its website, highlighting the appeal of training AI in space. However, the ample supply of solar energy is also great for cryptomining.
So, when Starcloud-2 reaches orbit, it will be tasked with raising some crypto-cash. In the embedded interview segment, Johnston said: “We’ll have some Bitcoin mining ASICs on the second spacecraft launching later this year.” At the time of writing 1BTC is worth roughly $86,000, quite a way down from highs several months ago.
Starcloud-2 is just the second of four currently planned satellite launches from the startup. It is framed as the company's first commercial mission, and like the prior satellite, will feature a GPU cluster. Interestingly, the official Starcloud-2 project page doesn’t mention Bitcoin mining or ASICs, so Johnston’s reveal is quite eyebrow-raising. Moreover, for something that seems a bit like an afterthought, “Potentially it [Bitcoin mining] is one of the most compelling use cases of space compute,” the Starcloud CEO told Documenting Bitcoin.
Johnson provided some financial insight into why there is now a Bitcoin side gig or pivot being considered. He cited the lower costs of ASICs vs. GPUs: they are about 30x cheaper than GPUs per kilowatt, he told the host. A specific example given was a 1KW Nvidia B200 chip at $30,000 vs. a 1KW ASIC at $1,000. Solving the energy supply situation in space for GPUs, or for ASICs, isn’t relevant to the business, said Johnson. We wonder what Nvidia will think about that.
While the availability of near-uninterrupted solar power is a big attraction of space-based compute, there are downsides. For example, satellites aren’t easy to service, and convection cooling doesn’t work in a vacuum. Commercial space-based data centers are so new that some of the problems and solutions will only become entirely clear after pioneering deployments like the Starcloud-2.

articles.title: Adobe Premiere finally brings powerful video editing to Android, and it's free
articles.text:
Video editing has never been Android’s strong suit. While Apple has long offered iMovie for iPhone and iPad, Google has never had a comparable offering. Adobe is now stepping up to fill this feature gap with a proper version of Premiere. The app is now available in the Play Store for almost all Android devices, and it’s free (mostly).
Android’s version of Premiere doesn’t offer all the features you’d get in the desktop application, but it’s a big step up from the soon-to-be-retired Premiere Rush app. You can import as many video tracks as you want, trim them, split them, add effects, and export videos in up to 4K resolution. It can even extract audio from clips, reduce background noise, and add voiceovers. The app emphasizes the YouTube Short format, even defaulting your video outputs to portrait 16:9, but you can change that to something more traditional.
On a standard smartphone, the app splits the screen with the timeline at the bottom and preview up top. Adobe says that Premiere is optimized for multiple form factors. If you have a foldable phone, the UI adjusts to give you more breathing room, placing the timeline to the right of the video. That makes sense as the default, as Premiere wants you to make YouTube Shorts, but if you’re working with something wider, there’s a layout toggle that puts the widescreen video above the expanded timeline. The split is also adjustable if you want to make your video or timeline larger.

articles.title: KI-Boom macht Menschen zu Milliardären
articles.text:
Alle U40 und aus der KI-Branche: Diese 7 Milliardäre sind neu im Club der Überreichen
In den vergangenen zwölf Monaten haben die 400 reichsten US-Amerikaner:innen zusammen ihre Vermögen um 1,4 Billionen Dollar vermehrt. Insgesamt stehen bei den Mitgliedern des Forbes-400-Rankings jetzt acht Billionen Dollar zu Buche – neuer Rekord. Wer es in den exklusiven Club der Überreichen schaffen will, benötigt schon mindestens 4,4 Milliarden Dollar.
Junge KI-Milliardäre neu in Forbes 400
Der Reichste der Reichen ist nach wie vor Elon Musk. Sein Vermögen beziffert Forbes mit 908 Milliarden Dollar. Auf den Plätzen folgen Jeff Bezos (378 Milliarden Dollar) und Larry Page (278 Milliarden Dollar). Spannender wird es, wenn man sich etwas tiefer in die Statistik gräbt und die Neuzugänge genauer unter die Lupe nimmt.
Der KI-Boom hat nämlich eine ganze Reihe Vertreter:innen von KI-Firmen in das Ranking der Überreichen gespült, darunter vergleichsweise junge Menschen. Insgesamt haben sieben Unternehmer:innen den Sprung ins Forbes 400 geschafft, die alle jünger als 40 Jahre sind und ihre Milliarden im KI-Bereich verdient haben.
Anthropic-Mitgründer steigen ins Ranking ein
Allein vier der sieben neuen KI-Milliardär:innen haben im Jahr 2021 gemeinsam Anthropic gegründet, wie Leadersnet schreibt. Daniela Amodei und Tom Brown (beide 39), Jack Clark (37) sowie Sam McCandlish (36) sollen jeweils über ein Vermögen von 15,5 Milliarden Dollar verfügen.
Zehn Milliarden Dollar mehr als die Anthropic-Gemeinde soll der 37-jährige OpenAI-Mitgründer Greg Brockman auf der hohen Kante haben. Neu im Ranking finden sich zudem der Surge-AI-Gründer Edwin Chen (38) und der 30-jährige Cognition-Mitgründer Steven Hao. Letzterer ist zugleich das jüngste Mitglied des Forbes-400-Rankings 2026.
Selfmade-Milliardäre statt Milliardärserben
Auffallend ist, dass nur eine der zehn jüngsten Mitglieder der Liste, Walmart-Nachkomme Lukas Walton, sein Vermögen geerbt hat. Mit 44,4 Milliarden Dollar ist er aber zugleich der reichste U40-Milliardär der USA. Die Gruppe vervollständigen Robinhood-Mitgründer Vlad Tenev und Anduril-Gründer Palmer Luckey.
Anders als in den USA stammen Milliardenvermögen in Deutschland – wie bei Lukas Walton – meist aus Unternehmensbeteiligungen innerhalb wohlhabender Familien. So tummeln sich mehrere deutsche Milliardär:innen in der Forbes-Liste der jüngsten Überreichen, darunter die Geschwister Johannes, Franz, Maximilian und Katharina von Baumbach (Boehringer Ingelheim).
Deutsche mit Milliardenvermögen
Zu den wenigen Ausnahmen gehören Alexander Rinke, Bastian Nominacher und Martin Klenk, wie die Frankfurter Rundschau schreibt. Die drei Selfmade-Milliardäre hatten 2011 an der TU München das Softwareunternehmen Celonis gegründet, das 13 Milliarden Dollar wert sein soll. Sie halten jeweils 15 Prozent an der Firma.

articles.title: Apple quiere plantarle cara a Whoop con una pulsera que no tiene pantalla
articles.text:
Apple está trabajando en una nueva pulsera de acondicionamiento físico que competirá directamente con Whoop. Según reporta el periodista Mark Gurman, los de Cupertino llevan meses desarrollando diversos prototipos, por lo que su llegada sería inminente. El proyecto ha sido respaldado por el mismo Tim Cook, antiguo CEO que cedió la dirección de la compañía a John Ternus.
De acuerdo con Bloomberg, la Apple Band sería una pulsera fitness sin pantalla muy parecida a lo que ya ofrece Whoop. Aunque el proyecto se encuentra en sus primeros pasos, el equipo ya pasó de la fase de ideas al desarrollo de prototipos funcionales. En esta fase, conocida internamente como investigación tecnológica, los ingenieros de Cupertino evalúan el desempeño de los prototipos para saber si pueden materializarse en un dispositivo final.
En términos de diseño, la banda está fabricada en tela fina e incluye un módulo con sensores. A diferencia del Apple Watch, esta pulsera no incluye pantalla y se enfoca solo en lo esencial, por lo que no competirán entre sí. El reloj inteligente cuenta con muchas funciones que ayudan al acondicionamiento físico, pero Apple busca algo más discreto, sin distracciones, y que pueda usarse en el día a día como la Whoop.
Aunque Tim Cook y Eddy Cue apoyan esta pulsera de fitness, no existe garantía de que se convertirá en un producto. Si la empresa decide seguir adelante, la Apple Band no se lanzará antes de 2028. Los de Cupertino tienen que evaluar más a fondo el desempeño y saber si se puede integrar con sus servicios, así como también sortear otros problemas como los que ocurren con la cadena de producción por culpa de la IA.
Apple no quiere depender solo del Apple Watch
Una pulsera inteligente hace sentido para Apple, sobre todo si consideramos el avance de Whoop en este campo. A diferencia del Apple Watch, que incluye todas las funciones y seguimiento de acondicionamiento físico, una pulsera con sensores como la de Whoop funciona a través de una suscripción. Aquí el usuario paga una tarifa mensual por comprar el dispositivo a menor coste y con acceso total a la plataforma.
Este esquema de suscripción garantizaría una entrada de dinero constante para Apple, algo que no obtiene cuando alguien compra el Apple Watch. Debido a que se trata de una membresía, la compañía "amarra" al usuario por un año o el tiempo que elija para pagar el dispositivo. Este mismo modelo lo aplica Oura, el anillo inteligente que registra tus métricas de sueño, ritmo cardíaco y otros valores de salud.
Una evidencia que anticipa la llegada de esta pulsera es que Apple ya comenzó a incorporar funciones al estilo Whoop en su app de Salud. Entre las novedades encontramos un seguimiento más preciso de tu frecuencia cardiaca y un modo que analiza tu nivel de preparación física para el día a día. Además, la app estrenó una nueva interfaz de usuario más limpia y accesible, inspirada en lo que ofrecen sus principales rivales.
Con la apuesta por la pulsera inteligente, Apple ha puesto el freno a otro ambicioso proyecto con IA. Gurman menciona que la compañía pausó el desarrollo de un colgante inteligente equipado con cámara e impulsado por la nueva Siri. Este wearable podría visualizar tu entorno y responder preguntas de un modo parecido a un asistente inteligente como el que vimos en la película Her.
Por el momento no se sabe si este proyecto retomará su desarrollo o si quedará archivado, sobre todo después del fiasco del AI Pin de Humane.

articles.title: Xbox keeps cutting with 268 more layoffs, hands Halo to Activision
articles.text:
The Xbox bloodbath continues with another round of layoffs and an internal shuffle that puts the next Halo game in Activision’s hands.
In a public staff memo titled “Continuing our reset,” Xbox’s executive vice president and chief content officer Matt Booty outlined the changes. These include the elimination of 268 roles across Halo Studios and other first-party studios, Xbox Game Studios management, and the “central functions” team.
Next, Booty detailed how Xbox is reorganizing its studios. First, Activision will expand to include World’s Edge and Rare, as well as developing the next Halo title. Booty said development would be “led by a new, purpose-built team that is separate from ongoing development and plans for Call of Duty.” Meanwhile, a small team at Halo Studios will continue to support the current, in-market games.
Similarly, Bethesda will expand to include Obsidian, with Booty noting the studio will continue current projects like Grounded and the new Fallout game in collaboration with Bethesda Game Studios.
King, the developers behind Candy Crush, will expand to include Microsoft Casual Games.
Wrapping up the reorganizations, Booty said Playground and Turn 10 will merge into one studio focused on the Forza and Fable franchises.
Finally, Booty shared an update on Xbox’s studio divestitures, noting that Undead Labs transitioned “on similar terms” to Double Fine and award-winning Canadian developers Compulsion Games, but will still release State of Decay III day one on Game Pass.
However, Booty said that two agreements for Ninja Theory fell through, and Xbox will “begin consultation with employees on a proposed closure while continuing to explore other paths forward.” Xbox also expects consultations with Arkane to continue through the end of the year.
The new round of layoffs and restructuring comes as part of the 3,200 total cuts Xbox detailed back in July. At the time, Xbox said it was cutting 1,600 employees immediately and another 1,600 over the next 12 months. In other words, there are more cuts to come, which makes Booty’s sign-off about looking ahead to “one of the strongest game lineups in our history” feel particularly tone deaf.
Amid the cuts, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma keeps talking about growing Microsoft’s gaming division with goals of reaching 500 million people every day by 2030 — nearly five times what Sharma says Xbox currently reaches. But it’s not clear how the company could do that when it continues gutting studios and laying off the people who would make the games Xbox needs to hit those kinds of numbers.
