articles.title: Changesets v3: Bumps Peer Dependents by Patch and Ships ESM Only with an 88% Smaller Install
articles.text:
Changesets, the file based versioning and changelog tool for JavaScript monorepos, has shipped v3.0, its first major release in the seven years since v2, bringing leaner installs, a rebuilt CLI, and a long awaited change to how peer dependencies are bumped.
The release landed on 11 August 2026, led by a refreshed maintainer team of Mateusz Burzyński, Bjorn Lu and Adam Haglund working through a public v3 release plan. It arrives with a new documentation site, a matching changesets/action v2, and more than 3M weekly downloads behind it.
All packages are now ESM only and require Node.js 22.11 or newer, plus pnpm 10, npm 10.9 or Yarn 4.5.2 as a minimum, with Yarn Classic dropped. The cleanup cut install size from 16.1MB to 2.1MB and dependencies from 95 to 39, and internally the project moved to tsdown, rolldown, vitest and oxfmt. Changelog formatting no longer pulls in its own Prettier copy, instead using @changesets/format to detect prettier, oxfmt, deno or dprint in the project.
The headline behaviour change is that a peer dependency update now gives dependents a patch bump rather than a major one. The old behaviour generated years of complaints, including issue 1011, where a team maintaining a design system monorepo wrote that bumping to a major version "feels like it is sending the wrong message and not honouring semver". Authors shipping a genuine break can still add an explicit major changeset for the dependent.
The maintainers of Bumpy, a recently launched competitor, note that v3 "hardcodes the opposite extreme", since every peer change is now assumed non breaking, and that neither version lets you configure propagation. Their comparison still credits v3 with fixing many long standing complaints, while listing gaps such as pnpm catalog support and an unchanged prerelease design.
The CLI was rebuilt on cac for argument parsing and clack prompts for interaction, which also fixes cancelled prompts crashing the process. New pack and publish-plan commands support the build, pack and publish sequence recommended by the e18e community, and the v2 action exposes sub actions so teams using npm trusted publishing can narrow publish permissions.
Upgrading is mostly configuration work, documented in the migration guide. Beyond the install requirements, commands and flags have been renamed:
# v2
changeset tag
changeset status --sinceMaster
# v3
changeset git-tag
changeset status --since=main
Configuration moves too, with prettier replaced by format and private packages no longer versioned unless opted back in:
{
 "format": "auto",
 "privatePackages": { "version": true, "tag": false }
}
changeset version now exits with code 1 when there is nothing to release, so as one team's release playbook warns, "any script that runs it unconditionally under set -e will now fail on an empty release".
Against semantic-release, which infers versions from conventional commits, and release-it, Changesets keeps its distinctive trade off that contributors write release intent into markdown files, and the release stays reviewable as a pull request. v3 does not change that model, it makes it cheaper to install and better behaved around peer dependencies.
Changesets is an MIT licensed tool for managing versioning and changelogs with a focus on monorepos. Contributors declare how their changes should be released, and the CLI turns those declarations into version bumps, changelog entries and registry publishes. v3 is available now, with v2 kept on a maintenance branch.

articles.title: 27,99 € pour la fibre et la TV 4K : SFR joue la carte de l’offre complète à petit prix
articles.text:
Entre les débits toujours plus élevés, le Wi-Fi de dernière génération et les bouquets de streaming intégrés, les offres Internet se sont largement étoffées ces dernières années. Mais tous les foyers n’ont pas nécessairement besoin d’abonnements fibre aussi sophistiqués et souvent plus chers que la moyenne.
Avec sa Fibre Starter, SFR propose une approche plus simple : fournir une connexion fibre suffisamment rapide pour les usages courants, tout en intégrant une véritable offre de télévision. Le tout pour rester sous la barre des 30 euros par mois.
Une connexion fibre jusqu’à 1 Gb/s pour 27,99 euros par mois
L’offre SFR Fibre Starter est actuellement proposée à 27,99 euros par mois, avec un engagement de 12 mois. Un abonnement qui inclut la location de la SFR Box 7, permettant d’obtenir un débit jusqu’à 1 Gb/s en téléchargement comme en envoi (sous réserve d’éligibilité de votre ligne). Elle adopte la norme Wi-Fi 5.
Ce débit symétrique couvre aisément les habitudes d’un logement. Plusieurs personnes peuvent regarder des vidéos en streaming, télécharger des jeux, effectuer des appels vidéo ou travailler à distance sans ressentir de ralentissements. De son côté, le gigabit en envoi est bien utile pour faire des sauvegardes dans le cloud ou envoyer des fichiers volumineux.
La téléphonie fixe est également incluse dans l’abonnement, avec les appels illimités vers les fixes en France métropolitaine, dans les DOM et vers plus de 100 destinations. SFR ajoute enfin son service Navigation Protégée, destiné à bloquer l’accès à certains domaines identifiés comme malveillants.
Un décodeur 4K et 160 chaînes directement inclus
L’abonnement Fibre Starter de SFR donne aussi accès à la télévision avec le décodeur SFR Box 7 TV. Il est compatible 4K et comprend un bouquet de 160 chaînes et services TV.
SFR mise encore sur le décodeur TV plutôt que sur une application à télécharger. Vous n’avez donc pas besoin de disposer d’un téléviseur récent avec un accès à une boutique d’applications pour profiter de la télévision. Il est néanmoins possible de télécharger l’application SFR TV pour profiter du bouquet télé depuis un smartphone ou une tablette.
Le décodeur donne accès à la télévision en direct, au replay et aux contenus à la demande. On retrouve aussi un guide TV, le contrôle du direct ainsi que la fonction Restart sur les chaînes compatibles, pour reprendre depuis le début une émission déjà commencée. L’offre Starter comprend par ailleurs huit heures d’enregistrement.
Les principales plateformes de streaming peuvent aussi être retrouvées depuis l’interface du décodeur. Leurs abonnements ne sont toutefois pas compris dans l’offre.
Pour un foyer qui regarde encore régulièrement les chaînes traditionnelles, le décodeur permet ainsi de réunir la télévision linéaire, le replay et les plateformes de vidéo dans la même interface.
Changer de fournisseur Internet est un jeu d’enfant
Quitter son fournisseur d’accès peut sembler contraignant, mais la procédure a été largement simplifiée en France, notamment grâce à la portabilité du numéro fixe.
Si vous souhaitez conserver votre numéro, il suffit de récupérer son RIO, un identifiant composé de 12 caractères. Celui-ci peut être obtenu en appelant gratuitement le 3179 depuis la ligne fixe concernée. Le RIO doit ensuite être communiqué au nouvel opérateur au moment de la souscription.
Dans ce cas, il ne faut pas résilier soi-même son ancienne offre : le nouvel opérateur se charge de la conservation du numéro et de la résiliation auprès de l’ancien fournisseur. Le contrat précédent prend fin lors du portage effectif du numéro.
SFR propose également de rembourser jusqu’à 100 euros de frais de résiliation ou de rupture d’engagement facturés par l’ancien opérateur.
La dernière étape consiste à restituer l’ancien matériel et à installer la nouvelle box. Notez que SFR facture les frais d’ouverture de service à hauteur de 49 euros. Cela comprend notamment le déplacement d’un technicien pour raccorder votre logement à la fibre.

articles.title: Test du Mac Studio M5 Max : un silence de cathédrale pour des performances qui explosent les records
articles.text:
Le Mac Studio est de retour pour clôturer le line-up 2026 d'Apple. La station de travail fixe embarque la puce M5 Max, toujours pensée pour répondre aux besoins des créateurs de contenu et amateurs d'IA locale.
On pensait terminer l'année 2026 sans lui, mais voilà que le Mac Studio est de retour pour exploser les benchmarks de notre comparatif de PC de bureau.
Si c'est son petit frère, l’Apple Mac mini, qui reçoit la primeur de la nouvelle puce M6, dont les secrets sont à retrouver dans notre test, nous avons opté pour le M5 Max pour la brique Studio. Toujours destinée aux créatifs, ingénieurs et autres professionnels de l'IA, cette machine s'appuie sur un silicium qui n'a rien d'inédit, puisqu'il est disponible dans le MacBook Pro depuis presque un an. Nonobstant, nous ne l'avions pas encore accueilli dans le comparatif des Numériques ; c'est désormais chose faite avec notre configuration de test.
Cette configuration ne fait pas dans la dentelle, puisqu'avec 128 Go de mémoire vive unifiée, 4 To de stockage et la version 40 cœurs GPU de la puce M5 Max, la facture finale arrive au chiffre impressionnant de 7839 €. Avec des caractéristiques plus modestes, à savoir la puce M5 Max dotée de 32 cœurs graphiques, 36 Go de RAM et 1 To de stockage, le prix de départ du Mac Studio est de 2999 €. Du reste, nous ne ferons pas l'étalage des nouveautés par rapport au Mac Studio M4 Max, puisque ces dernières sont réduites à peau de chagrin pour ce millésime 2026. Faisons le point.
Que dire de la conception de ce Mac Studio 2026 qui n'ait pas déjà été formulé l'an passé ? Pas grand-chose, à vrai dire. Le pavé d'aluminium conserve des mensurations strictement identiques (19,7 x 19,7 x 9,5 cm) pour un poids inchangé de 2,7 kg. Une stagnation logique, puisqu'il incarne désormais le standard esthétique des ordinateurs de bureau signés Apple.
Il en va de même pour la connectique, figée dans le marbre : la façade accueille toujours deux ports USB-C (Gen 3.2) et un lecteur de cartes SD, tandis que le panneau arrière aligne quatre ports Thunderbolt 5, deux ports USB-A, un port HDMI 2.1, un port RJ45 10 Gb/s et une sortie casque. En clair, nul besoin de bouleverser l'ergonomie de votre bureau si vous sautez le pas depuis la génération précédente. On note tout de même une bonne nouvelle sur le front du réseau sans-fil : la machine s'offre enfin le luxe de la modernité en intégrant les normes wifi 7 et Bluetooth 6.
Quelles que soient les tâches parallèles que l'on impose à ce Mac Studio, l'ordinateur encaisse le choc sans jamais se départir de son silence de cathédrale. Seul un murmure trahit son fonctionnement si l'on tend l'oreille attentivement, notre sonomètre ayant d'ailleurs péniblement relevé un souffle de 32,7 dB.
Pour véritablement tirer la large ventilation de son sommeil, nous avons dû dégainer Prime95, un stress test bien connu des bidouilleurs, chargé de saturer les 18 cœurs logiques à leur paroxysme. Si cette torture numérique demeure très éloignée d'un usage concret (et n'est mentionnée ici qu'à titre indicatif), elle aura tout de même réussi à propulser la consommation énergétique à 144 W (flirtant ainsi avec son TDP maximal de 145 W) et à faire grimper les sondes internes jusqu'à 85 °C. Une chauffe exceptionnelle qui s'est accompagnée d'une accélération audible des ventilateurs, mais circonscrite à une petite vingtaine de secondes.
Avec ses 18 cœurs de calcul logiques et 40 cœurs graphiques, le M5 Max du Mac Studio prend sans grande surprise la tête de notre comparatif des PC de bureau. Malgré cet état de fait, l'écart entre les indices CPU du silicium M6 du tout récent Mac mini s'avère moins large que prévu, puisque ce dernier talonne (136) le M5 Max (140).
Pour rappel, les atouts du Mac Studio se jouent dans les tâches multithreadées, à savoir la création de contenu qui a pour habitude de solliciter plusieurs cœurs de calcul en simultané. Comme l'explique la communication de la Pomme, c'est une bécane pensée pour le montage, l'édition vidéo ou la modélisation 3D. Un fait attesté par les benchmarks applicatifs où le M5 Max tient une nette avance sur la concurrence, autant sur la suite Adobe que sur le rendu 3D via Blender, fort d'une optimisation logicielle sans pareille.
En jeu aussi, le M5 Max marque une belle évolution par rapport au M4 Max, puisque notre benchmark sur Shadow of the Tomb Raider (préréglage Très élevé, définition Full HD) affiche une moyenne de 178 i/s contre 137 i/s pour son prédécesseur. Il reste néanmoins toujours derrière le Framework Desktop et son puissant APU AMD Ryzen AI 300, ce dernier conservant l'avantage en gaming grâce à sa large compatibilité et sa flexibilité dans le rendu en temps réel.
Sans benchmark IA établi, il nous est impossible de mesurer concrètement les avancées du Neural Engine sur les tâches liées à l'intelligence artificielle, qu'il s'agisse de l'inférence ou de l'entraînement de modèles.
Ainsi, le benchmark théorique de Geekbench AI ne montre pas de différence flagrante entre le M5 Max et le M4 Max, ce dernier affichant même un score en précision simple FP32 (6502) — alias la puissance brute théorique — supérieur à la nouvelle puce (6235).
Néanmoins, le M5 Max le dépasse en demi-précision FP16 (42 117) et en quantification (66 260), deux scores importants pour l'inférence de LLM locaux. La présence d'un accélérateur neuronal dans chacun des 16 cœurs du Neural Engine (absent sur le M4 Max) creuse potentiellement l'écart dans une utilisation concrète d'applications de type LM Studio.
Notre constat consacré au châssis du Mac Studio s'applique aussi à la partie audio puisque les enceintes intégrées du millésime 2026 sont toujours aussi bruyantes, à défaut d'être particulièrement agréables à l'oreille de par l'absence de basses et leur orientation désavantageuse.
Toutefois, la sortie casque est toujours de très bonne facture, Apple oblige, comme l'indiquent les mesures relevées par notre analyseur. Ainsi, le Mac Studio (2026) profite d'une distorsion contenue à 0,001 % et un niveau de sortie à 363 mV RMS tout à fait supérieur à la moyenne des PC testés. La plage dynamique à 110 dB et la diaphonie à -60 dB sont largement suffisantes pour une bonne restitution des effets stéréo.
|  | Apple Mac Studio (2026) | Moyenne des PC testés | 
|---|---|---|
| Niveau de sortie | 363 mVRMS | 300 mVRMS | 
| Distorsion + bruit | 0,001 % | 0,006 % | 
| Plage dynamique | 110 dB | 100 dB | 
| Diaphonie | -60 dB | -44 dB | 
Toujours aussi puissant et compact, le Mac Studio revient en forme pour cette itération 2026. Si l'écart avec la génération précédente est moins marqué qu'attendu, la station de travail reprend la tête de notre comparatif d'ordinateurs fixes. Las, le ticket d'entrée est, cette fois-ci, encore plus élevé que par le passé. Le prix du luxe en 2026 !

articles.title: Google's Googlebook isn't a better Chromebook, it's an attempt to rebuild the PC around Android
articles.text:
Looking ahead: Google has completely pulled back the curtain on its replacement for the Chromebook platform, designed to tackle Windows and macOS head-on. The upcoming notebooks from Acer, Asus, Dell, HP, and Lenovo aim to bring the Android software stack to a full-blown PC operating system for Arm and x86 devices.
Pre-orders are now open for the first Googlebook laptops from five manufacturers. Starting prices range from $899 to $1,299.
Google is positioning the notebooks as the ultimate companions for Android phone owners. When a user first signs into a Googlebook, it can instantly import the phone's settings, saved passwords, and Wi-Fi connections.
Similar to how Macs can access all the files and apps on a user's iPhone, a Googlebook can seamlessly summon an Android phone's files and messages. Users can start a task on a mobile app and continue on the Googlebook. The machines combine the Android and Chromebook environments by natively supporting Android apps alongside a desktop-grade Chrome experience, complete with extensions.
Unsurprisingly, Google's AI assistant, Gemini, is at the core of the OS. Wiggling the mouse summons the assistant to answer questions and complete various tasks. A dedicated button, called Rambler, also transcribes spoken words into headers, checklists, formatted takeaways, and other documents. Users can also use prompts to create custom widgets or build apps through the Antigravity AI agent platform.
Each Googlebook includes a year of Google AI Pro and three months of YouTube Premium, Adobe Photoshop, and more. Google promises to provide up to a decade of content and feature updates.
The Dell and HP Googlebooks run on Snapdragon X Elite processors, while Intel Core Ultra 5 chips serve as the baseline for the others, and all of the SoCs include NPUs that achieve up to 45 TOPs. With a 13.4-inch 2.5K LCD touchscreen, Dell's XPS Googlebook is the smallest. The others sport 14-inch 2.8K OLED panels, except Lenovo's, which measures 15.3 inches. Starting models all include 16GB of RAM and 512GB of storage, and some are upgradeable to 32GB of memory.
Other features include backlit keyboards, haptic trackpads, and Google's Glowbar, which displays patterns in response to boot cycles, battery level, and AI actions. Google's Titan C2 security chip supports fingerprint readers on all models, while the HP and Lenovo notebooks also include facial unlock. The laptops also feature aluminum, magnesium alloy, and carbon fiber chassis.
Googlebooks will be available starting October 4 in the US and October 5 in Canada, the UK, Ireland, France, Germany, and Australia.

articles.title: The companies that were never fundable are now buildable | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Ask a European founder how the company is going and you’ll usually hear a number of answers. Ask an investor how a portfolio company is progressing and headcount will often be among the first three metrics.
For thirty years, that shorthand worked because software output was closely tied to the number of people building it. That relationship has now broken. But the way startups are funded, and the metrics investors use to assess them, has not caught up.
Consider what a small team can now carry: a production backend, a rendering engine, the tooling around them, an on-device AI component, and a commercial operation running live deployments in more than one country. Teams of under a dozen are doing this now.
Five years ago that scope would have required a team several times the size, and the difference is not that today’s engineers are cleverer. It is that the parts of the job which used to consume most of the headcount, the writing of ordinary code, the wiring of one system to another, the second and third implementations of the same thing, have become cheap.
This is not a productivity story. Those are boring and mostly over-claimed. It is a story about which companies are now possible, and that is a different and more interesting question.
When software gets cheap, markets get smaller
The category that changes most is the one venture capital has always struggled with: products serving markets of tens of thousands rather than tens of millions. Such businesses were not previously un-buildable, they were un-fundable, because the engineering cost floor sat above what the market could return.
A fund needs outcomes large enough to matter against the whole portfolio, so founders were steered toward categories with enough headroom to justify the build. Plenty of useful things were never made for that reason alone.
Lower the floor and those products come into range. They can be built by four people, reach profitability at a scale that would embarrass a growth investor, and serve a market properly for years. What they cannot do is return a fund.
Europe is unusually well positioned for this, and not for the reason usually given.
The standard line is that Europe should stop apologising for building smaller companies. That is sentimental. The actual argument is structural: Europe has fewer megafunds, more fragmented markets that reward specificity over scale, and a large population of technical founders who would rather own most of a real business than a sliver of a speculative one. Those were disadvantages when the cost floor was high. They are not obviously disadvantages now.
The practical consequence for founders is that the hiring question has changed. The useful question is no longer how many engineers you need to build the thing. It is which of your constraints was ever a headcount constraint, because several of them were not and some no longer are.
Teams that hire to signal progress to investors will find they have bought coordination overhead rather than capability, and coordination overhead is the one cost that has not fallen at all.
For investors the harder adjustment is diligence. If headcount no longer indicates capability, it stops being a useful signal, and the substitutes are more work: what has actually shipped, what is in production rather than in the deck, what happens when the clever parts fail. Those questions were always better. They were just more expensive to ask than counting people.
Headcount was never the whole company
Anyone making this argument should be straight about the cost, because small teams are worse at some things.
Small teams have little slack, and slack is where the unglamorous work gets done. Every consumer product has a retention problem it knows about and has not fixed, and in a company of ten the reason is never that the diagnosis is hard. It is that nobody has a week free from something more immediately pressing.
In a company of a hundred, that problem is somebody’s entire job and it gets solved. Cheap code does not change this. It arguably makes it worse, because it becomes easy to build the next thing instead of finishing the last one.
That is the honest shape of it. The floor has dropped, which widens what can be attempted, and it does nothing about focus, judgement or the discipline to complete things. Those remain expensive, they remain human, and they are now a larger share of what separates companies that work from companies that merely exist.
The measure worth watching is not how many people a company employs. It is what it has shipped, what it has finished, and what it has chosen not to do.

articles.title: Medo da IA no Brasil supera média global, diz pesquisa • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Medo da IA no Brasil supera média global, diz pesquisa
Pesquisa aponta 52% da população receosa com o futuro da tecnologia, mas um quarto da população nunca nem ouviu falar.
O futuro da inteligência artificial vem tirando o sono de mais da metade dos brasileiros. Pelo menos é o que aponta a pesquisa mais recente sobre o tema feita pela Pew Research Center. Os dados mostram um aumento na média global de pessoas preocupadas com os avanços da IA: em todo o mundo, 37% declararam ter mais receio que expectativa com a tecnologia. No Brasil, esse número sobe para 52%.
O medo dos mais jovens em relação à IA também vem numa crescente em países como Estados Unidos, Austrália, Japão e Brasil. Por aqui, já são 12% a mais de pessoas entre 18 e 34 anos levando preocupações com a IA em conta desde 2025. Mas, considerando um recorte global, a maior parte dos entrevistados (48%) nessa faixa etária vê a IA com certo equilíbrio.
Outro dado interessante é sobre as preocupações que relacionam IA à desigualdade social. Para 28% dos entrevistados, a tecnologia vai aumentar a diferença entre ricos e pobres. Aqui no Brasil, a maioria (30%) não vê dessa forma, enquanto 24% das pessoas acreditam que sim. A pesquisa foi realizada em 37 países de diferentes continentes entre março e junho.
Segundo os dados da Pew Research Center, o Brasil fica abaixo apenas de Austrália e Estados Unidos quando o assunto é preocupação com inteligência artificial. Além disso, é o país com menor percentual de pessoas animadas com o tema (8%), contrastando com os 52% que veem o assunto com receio.
Chama atenção também o fato de a preocupação ser mais comum entre pessoas acima dos 50 anos aqui no Brasil (58%), enquanto os jovens representam 44% desse recorte. Vale reforçar aqui que o Brasil está entre os seis países que registraram um aumento desse receio na faixa etária de 18 a 34 anos, saindo de 32% em 2025.
O impacto da inteligência artificial no mercado de trabalho é uma das principais preocupações atuais, sobretudo entre os jovens. Nos Estados Unidos, por exemplo, 74% das pessoas entre 18 e 34 anos acreditam em uma oferta menor de empregos relacionada ao crescimento da IA.
Vale lembrar que em maio deste ano algumas formaturas nos EUA tiveram vaias para executivos do mercado de tecnologia. Além disso, no último mês, uma pesquisa da CNBC junto ao Generation Labs apontou mais de 70% de desconfiança dos jovens em líderes da IA.
Aqui no Brasil, o percentual de pessoas preocupadas com os impactos da IA no mercado de trabalho chega a 42% em todas as faixas analisadas. Mas também há quem acredite num aumento de oportunidades com a tecnologia: 13% veem desta forma. Os países com maior índice de receio no tema são Austrália e Coreia do Sul, ambos om 76%, enquanto os EUA vêm logo atrás, com 71%.
Essa talvez seja a informação mais curiosa do levantamento feito pela Pew Research Center. Segundo os dados da pesquisa, são 27% dos brasileiros que afirmam nunca terem ouvido falar de IA. A maioria (42%) diz conhecer pouco do assunto, enquanto 31% dizem saber bastante sobre o tema. Nossos vizinhos da Argentina também têm um bom número de pessoas alheias à IA, com 30%.
Em relação à pesquisa feita em 2025, mais pessoas já ouviram falar ou leram sobre IA por aqui. O Brasil está entre os países em que esse percentual mais cresceu, subindo de 22% para os 31% registrados em 2026. Segundo os dados do estudo, o conhecimento sobre inteligência artificial é maior entre os países mais ricos – o que estaria relacionado à maior facilidade de acesso.

articles.title: X de Elon Musk lanza función para avisar a usuarios cuando un país limitó la visibilidad de sus publicaciones o cuenta
articles.text:
X amplió Under The Hood con una función que muestra si la visibilidad de una cuenta o de sus publicaciones fue limitada por el cumplimiento obligatorio de leyes locales.
Under The Hood es una herramienta de transparencia de la red social de Musk que permite a los usuarios consultar las etiquetas aplicadas a sus cuentas y publicaciones. Esas etiquetas, como spam, contenido para adultos o conducta de odio, pueden limitar el alcance de los posteos en la sección “Para ti”.
PUBLICIDAD
La actualización permite saber si una publicación fue retenida en un país tras una exigencia legal y en qué territorio se aplicó esa restricción. Hasta ahora, la función mostraba las etiquetas aplicadas a cuentas y publicaciones durante el mes anterior.
Qué incluye la nueva medida de Under The Hood
La función, disponible en x.com/i/underthehood, incluye estadísticas sobre etiquetas como spam, contenido para adultos o conducta de odio.
Las cuentas que cumplan los requisitos de elegibilidad —más de 10 publicaciones en el mes anterior y al menos un año de antigüedad— pueden descargar un informe en formato JSON.
El archivo permite identificar perfiles sin marcas o publicaciones señaladas con etiquetas como NSFWHIGHRECALL y SPAMHIGHRECALL.
La herramienta también se integra con el código de clasificación de código abierto de X en GitHub. La ampliación busca que los usuarios comprendan el alcance de las restricciones aplicadas a sus publicaciones sin que la plataforma deba explicar cada factor de forma individual.
PUBLICIDAD
X anuncia que desmanteló red de bots chinos que publicaba contenido contra IA y centros de datos
X anunció que eliminó una red de 200.000 cuentas automatizadas vinculadas a China que difundía mensajes contra los centros de datos de inteligencia artificial en Estados Unidos. Según la plataforma, las publicaciones buscaban influir en el debate sobre política energética e IA.
Sin embargo, un análisis de Darren Linvill, investigador de la Universidad de Clemson, cuestionó el alcance de la operación: al menos 59 cuentas no habían tenido interacción con usuarios reales antes de ser suspendidas.
Linvill examinó publicaciones con el hashtag “capacityauction”, incluido en capturas divulgadas por X, y encontró 90 mensajes publicados en enero. Cada cuenta había posteado solo dos o tres veces antes de su suspensión. El investigador sostuvo que las publicaciones probablemente no llegaron a personas reales.
PUBLICIDAD
El caso se conoció mientras crece en Estados Unidos la oposición a los centros de datos de gran escala. Una encuesta de Gallup publicada en mayo indicó que más del 70% de los consultados rechazaba su instalación en sus comunidades por el consumo de energía y agua y por el rechazo a la IA.
Samuel Woolley, investigador de la Universidad de Pittsburgh, advirtió que ese movimiento tiene bases genuinas y bipartidistas, más allá de la influencia extranjera y de las campañas detectadas por las plataformas tecnológicas en general.
Elon Musk destaca a Anthropic frente a OpenAI
Elon Musk afirmó que Anthropic presta más atención a la seguridad de la inteligencia artificial que OpenAI, aunque advirtió que ninguna empresa del sector está exenta de riesgos.
PUBLICIDAD
Durante su participación en All-In Summit, el propietario de X propuso que las principales compañías sometan sus modelos a evaluaciones cruzadas antes de lanzarlos al público.
El empresario planteó que las firmas compartan acceso anticipado a sus sistemas mediante una interfaz de programación de aplicaciones (API). Así, sus competidores podrían aplicar pruebas propias para detectar vulnerabilidades y alertar sobre problemas no resueltos.
Musk consideró que este mecanismo ayudaría a identificar riesgos relacionados con armas biológicas o nucleares, conductas engañosas y otros usos maliciosos.
Musk sostuvo que Anthropic y OpenAI lideran la carrera por los modelos de lenguaje y tienen capacidades similares. A su juicio, esa competencia dificulta que una de las compañías reduzca el ritmo de desarrollo sin conceder una ventaja a su rival.
PUBLICIDAD
El dueño de X calificó de “algo imprudente” una prueba de seguridad atribuida a OpenAI, que utilizó miles de agentes de inteligencia artificial para intentar vulnerar sistemas informáticos. También cuestionó que las grandes compañías sean llamadas “laboratorios”, porque, según dijo, son corporaciones con fines de lucro.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Toyota orders workers to train humanoid robots but says humans won't be replaced
articles.text:
Toyota workers are already helping to train humanoid robots as part of the automaker’s race to eventually deploy 400,000 factory robots—but a Toyota executive said the robotic push is not meant to directly replace humans.
Starting in 2028, the Toyota Motor group aims to start investing $6.42 billion every year in upgrading factories with the new robotic workforce, according to Nikkei Asia. The company wants to put 150,000 robots in its own automotive plants and deploy another 250,000 at group company facilities that produce various components and materials.
Toyota has already begun deploying some of its ELEY humanoid robots across assembly lines to learn from human workers. Nikkei Asia reported that workers are teaching the robots, which roll around on wheels, to perform tasks requiring precise hand movements by wearing “jigs” based on the humanoids’ fingers.
That naturally raises questions about the future of the Japan-based automaker’s human workforce, which has 18,000 veteran workers across 60 factories worldwide, including 11 US manufacturing plants. But Hiroki Nakajima, a Toyota executive vice president, told Nikkei Asia that the company aims for “a world where robots coexist with humans, rather than replacing them.”
It’s unclear how many robots Toyota has already deployed overall or how many of the new robots will be humanoids. But the automotive industry has been a leading adopter of industrial robots for decades, with such robots typically being robotic arms installed at workstations and mobile robots that move components or materials around.
China alone deployed 2 million industrial robots in 2024, with Japan coming in second at 450,500 robots, according to the International Federation of Robotics. The United States and South Korea ranked third and fourth with 34,200 robots and 30,600 robots, respectively.

articles.title: Freedom Mobile to shutter 3G in part of Ontario next month
articles.text:
Canada’s ongoing 3G shutdown is coming to a new region next month.
Starting Oct. 17, 2026, Freedom Mobile says it will start shutting down 3G in the Peterborough, Ont., region. This comes after Freedom shuttered 3G in the Ottawa-Gatineau region and across Quebec in July, and in Manitoba last year. Notably, SaskTel is also set to shutter its 3G network in October.
Most Canadian wireless providers aim to shutter 3G networks by March 2027. Bell, Telus, and Freedom all cite that date on their respective 3G shutdown support pages, while Rogers completed its 3G shutdown last year.
Carriers are shutting down 3G in order to enhance LTE and 5G networks, but the move is impacting Canadians using older devices or ones that aren’t officially supported by Canadian carriers.
The core issue relates to Voice over LTE (VoLTE) technology, which is used to transmit phone calls over LTE networks. However, phones that don’t support VoLTE, either because they’re too old or because they’re not compatible with Canadian carriers’ VoLTE systems, fall back to 3G networks to make phone calls. That means those devices will no longer be able to place phone calls once the 3G network is retired.
Most Canadian carriers offer tools on their websites for users to check if their device is compatible with VoLTE. So, if you’re not sure, that’s a great place to start. For some people, the solution will be as simple as turning on VoLTE in their device’s settings app. Others may have to upgrade to a newer phone.
Unfortunately, Canadians carriers typically only ensure compatibility with the smartphones they sell, which has left some people in a lurch. For example, many OnePlus devices that are capable of VoLTE were facing issues during Rogers’ 3G shutdown last year. OnePlus ultimately pushed an update to address the problem, but it’s worth keeping in mind that some phone brands may face compatibility issues if they’re not available from Canadian carriers.

articles.title: ‘The best compact Dolby Atmos soundbar I've tested': the Sonos Beam Ultra offers incredibly immersive audio, excellent features, and a gorgeous design — here's how I rate it after a week of use
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Sonos Beam Ultra marries the compact nature of the standard Beam and the true Atmos credentials of the Arc to perfection to deliver expansive, immersive audio in a single slim package. Its elegant design and vast feature-suite only help to justify the asking price, although it would’ve been nice to see HDMI passthrough on board.
Pros
- +Up-firing drivers and amazing Atmos effects
- +Clear dialogue with effective Speech Enhancement
- +Compact and beautiful design
Cons
- -No HDMI passthrough
- -DTS:X left out
Why you can trust TechRadar
Sonos Beam Ultra review
The Sonos Beam Ultra doesn’t merely feel like an evolution of the pre-existing Beam products. Instead, it feels like something of a middle child between the Sonos Beam Gen 2 and the Sonos Arc Ultra. After all, it sits bang in between its sibling models when it comes to channel configuration, boasting a 7.1.2 setup with nine drivers, and while it has up-firing drivers for true Dolby Atmos, it still maintains a fairly compact design.
But the Beam Ultra certainly isn’t an awkward middle-child; it’s a highly capable mid-range option that provides striking cinematic sound, while still being able to fit into a smaller setup. But is the Sonos Beam Ultra worth its $699 / £699 / AU$1,099 asking price?
Like most of the best soundbars, the Sonos Beam Ultra supports Dolby Atmos (though notably Sonos omits DTS:X), and it handles the format very effectively. When watching a 4K UHD Blu-ray of The Mask, the soundbar seamlessly tracked the titular character as he tornadoes across the screen, with audio sounding as if it far exceeded the limited confines of the soundbar. When The Mask jumped upwards, diagonally, his upward trajectory was captured with precision.
And the Beam Ultra continued to impress me with its height effects across multiple movies. For instance, in Godzilla Minus One, the sense of a plane flying overhead was replicated more naturally than I expected from a mid-range bar. When Godzilla first appeared, the width of the kaiju’s movement was handled brilliantly — it sounded as if the creature’s stomping and destruction were emanating from different corners of the testing room, rather than a set of speakers, even without the help of surround speakers.
What’s more, the Sonos Beam Ultra nails the fundamentals. Watching Top Gun: Maverick, the roar of jet engines was palpable, and I found this to be the case across multiple films. For a mid-sized standalone bar, the Beam Ultra produces incredibly regimented, deep, and responsive low-end sound, which is excellent for movies with high-octane action sequences and dark, impactful scores. The Beam Ultra can also get seriously loud if you want to fill a more open space, but I never noticed any tinniness or harsh compression.
Still, this doesn’t come at the expense of sounds elsewhere in the frequency range. I found dialogue to be generally clear and detailed too, though I will note that turning on the Speech Enhancement mode and setting it to Medium gave me the best results. This means you can bring voices forward without hampering the fidelity of other elements in the mix.
The Beam Ultra even proved to be a hit for music, whether I was listening to an Atmos or stereo mix. With an Atmos mix of I’m Gonna Love You Just A Little More Baby by Barry White, there was tremendous width to the guitars, the vocals were perfectly clear in the center, and the bass had pleasant warmth to it. Moving over to First Summer by H.K., deep bass came through with attention-grabbing impact, sounding more full-sounding than I’d anticipated, yet keys and vocal chops in the mid-range still maintained excellent clarity, as did articulate drums in the treble.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The Sonos Beam Ultra isn’t just a great performer; it’s also rammed full of useful features. TruePlay is here, which can optimize sound for your room in mere seconds, but there are also ways to manually adapt audio. For instance, you can adjust height effects to your choosing, and there’s even a height-effect simulation mode if there’s less than four inches of space above your soundbar — ideal if you’re placing the Beam Ultra on a shelf in your TV stand, say.
I've already mentioned the Speech Enhancement mode, which has multiple levels to emphasize speech as little or much as you need, but there’s also a Night mode if you don’t want to disturb others. You can turn these options on in the Sonos app, but there’s also an option to add a voice assistant if you want to make adjustments on the fly.
The Beam Ultra can, as you'd expect, also interact with other components in your Sonos system. You can pair compatible speakers, such as the Sonos Play, and use them as surround speakers. TV Audio Swap is also back, and enables you to transfer sound from your Beam Ultra to your Sonos Ace or Sonos Ace Ultra headphones. I tried this out with the latter cans, and found that switching was speedy and responsive, while the quality of spatial audio was exceptional — make sure to read my Sonos Ace Ultra review for a deeper dive.
There are a fair few ways to connect to your Sonos Beam Ultra too. Of course, HDMI eARC is the most important — this is what you’ll use to hook the soundbar up to your TV and experience Dolby Atmos movies in all their glory. There’s also Wi-Fi 6 for streaming content over a local connection, allowing you to use services like Tidal Connect and Spotify Connect. And, unlike with the Beam Gen 2, you also get Bluetooth 5.3 connectivity as well as USB-C line-in.
One thing I would have really have loved to see, though, is an HDMI input, which has been left off of the Sonos Beam Ultra. Given that connecting the soundbar up to your TV already takes away one precious HDMI slot, it would’ve been great to get a passthrough port on this model — it’s something I use on my Marshall Heston 120 at home, given that I have multiple game consoles connected up.
Something that does not disappoint, though, is the Beam Ultra’s design. It’s sleek, modern, and stylish — but understated enough to seamlessly slot into just about any living space. It also has a great standard of build, intuitive touch controls, and handy status indicator lights to signify connection status. There’s also a microphone slider, which you can deactivate if you don’t want your soundbar listening in on you.
But here comes the big question: is the Sonos Beam Ultra actually worth the money? While $699 / £699 / AU$1,099 is by no means cheap, I still think the answer is yes. It’s priced right in between the Beam Gen 2 and Arc Ultra, and feels like a true best-of-both-worlds option — the height channels give it much more convincing Atmos performance than the Beam Gen 2, but you also get amazing power in a single, compact package.
Sure, you could get a soundbar and sub combo like the Samsung HW-Q800F for a similar price, and that will give you even deeper, more cinematic bass. But that model has a more restrictive 5.1.2 configuration, and if you want something more low-profile, it won’t fit the bill. You also get an excellent suite of features from the Beam Ultra, and you can add a compatible sub and other other Sonos speakers for surround sound if you wish.
As a result, the Sonos Beam Ultra might just be the best compact Dolby Atmos soundbar I’ve tested. In spite of its modest size, it plates up powerful, immersive, and clear audio, so if you want a simple plug-and-play solution to get amazing audio into just about any space, this is my top recommendation.

- Released in September 2026
The Sonos Beam Ultra is priced at $699 / £699 / AU$1,099, placing it mid-way between the Sonos Beam Gen 2 and the Sonos Arc Ultra. While you can get some multi-box options for a similar price, like the Sony HW-Q800F, for instance, the Beam Ultra features an extensive 7.1.2 driver configuration, and its compact nature is a central part of its appeal.

| Design | Stellar looks, slim build, neat touch controls. | 5/5 | 
| Setup & usability | Plug and play set-up, easy to connect to via Wi-Fi or Bluetooth. | 5/5 | 
| Value | Not cheap, but a perfect marriage of the standard Beam and Arc that’s priced accordingly. | 4.5/5 | 
Buy it if…
You want a compact soundbar with amazing Dolby Atmos
So many compact Dolby Atmos soundbars fall flat when it comes to Dolby Atmos. Often, that’s due to a lack of dedicated up-firing drivers to provide convincing height effects. But the Beam Ultra has those — and it also conjures up an impressive sense of width.
You already own a Sonos system
If you already have a compatible sub and speakers like the Sonos Play or Sonos Era 100, you can connect them to the Beam Ultra to open up even more immersive, three-dimensional audio. TV Audio Swap is also available if you’ve got the Sonos Ace or Sonos Ace Ultra headphones.
Don’t buy it if…
You need HDMI passthrough
The Sonos Beam Ultra does not offer HDMI passthrough, which might be troublesome if, like me, you have multiple games consoles, a 4K Blu-ray player, and other devices that use HDMI. 
You need DTS:X
The Sonos Beam Ultra supports Dolby Atmos, but not DTS:X, much like other Sonos soundbars, including the Sonos Arc Ultra. A number of 4K discs make use of DTS:X, so if you’re someone who often makes use of that format, it may be worth looking elsewhere.

articles.title: Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6: así es el nuevo chip de Qualcomm que llevará tu próximo móvil
articles.text:
Qualcomm sigue en su cruzada de ofrecer los mejores chips móviles del mercado. Y lo cierto es que, fuera del ecosistema de Apple, siguen siendo los más punteros y los más usados por los fabricantes que quieren llevar en sus móviles lo más potente del mercado. Ahora la compañía ha presentado el chip que será la referencia para el próximo curso: el Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 y su versión enfocada a la IA que lleva el nombre de Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6.
Ambos chips son lo más avanzado que ofrece Qualcomm hasta la fecha y ofrecen una combinación de alto rendimiento e inteligencia en el dispositivo con avances significativos para su uso en IA, videojuegos, cámara y conectividad.
En este sentido, el Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 está fabricado con el mismo proceso avanzado de 2 nm, cuenta con la CPU Qualcomm Oryon de diseño personalizado en combinación con su GPU Qualcomm Adreno y la NPU Qualcomm Hexagon. Esta integración permite que la nueva generación de SOC de Qualcomm ofrezca un enorme avance en términos de rendimiento para su uso con funciones de IA, videojuegos, procesamiento de imágenes y conectividad a cualquier móvil de gama alta que apueste por este chip.
Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 tendrá una versión Extreme enfocada en la IA
Además, Qualcomm ofrece también la versión Extreme Gen 6, enfocada a los fabricantes que quieran ofrecer en sus móviles funciones de IA mucho más avanzada. De hecho, esta versión Extreme ofrece un rendimiento para su uso en IA con más de 30 mil millones de parámetros en modelos MoE y hasta un 50% de memoria compartida adicional.
Esta versión de alto rendimiento incluye núcleos de matriz Adreno dedicados a la IA para la ejecución de modelos avanzados y Neural Fusion para su uso en superresolución y generación de fotogramas impulsadas por IA de 18 MB de HPM (memoria de alto rendimiento). Además, cuenta con compatibilidad con APV, soporte para vídeo en 8K60 y vídeo en cámara lenta Ultra HD a 240 cuadros por segundo.
Sobre su disponibilidad, se espera que todos los dispositivos de gama alta de nueva generación empiecen a montar Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 y Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 próximamente.

articles.title: Rewes KI-Chatbot: Vom ignorierten Tool zu 5.000 Anfragen im Monat
articles.text:
KI-Akzeptanz: Wie Rewe digital einfach nur den Chatbot umbenannte
Interne IT-Hotlines kommen an ihre Grenzen, je größer ein Unternehmen wird: Anfragen häufen sich, Bearbeitungszeiten steigen und das Vertrauen in den Support bröckelt. Bei der Rewe Group betraf das rund 20.000 Verwaltungsmitarbeitende und ihre Fragen von IT-Störungen bis zu neuer Hard- und Software.
Rewe digital, die IT-Einheit des Konzerns, entwickelte einen eigenen Chatbot: Er beantwortet Fragen direkt aus internen Wissensquellen und legt bei Bedarf automatisch ein Support-Ticket an. Eine Lösung von der Stange war keine Option. Erstens musste der Bot aus Compliance- und Datenschutzgründen dauerhaft in Europa laufen. Zweitens sollte er auf das Wissen zugreifen, das schon in Confluence und SharePoint lag, statt eine komplett neue Wissensbasis aufzubauen.
Technisch überzeugte der Chatbot von Anfang an. Trotzdem nutzte ihn kaum jemand.
KI-Akzeptanz als entscheidender Erfolgsfaktor für IT-Projekte
Damit steht Rewe digital für ein Muster, das laut Bitkom-Studienbericht 2026 viele Unternehmen kennen: Fast jedes dritte Unternehmen (31 Prozent) nennt fehlende Akzeptanz der Beschäftigten als eines der größten Hemmnisse beim KI-Einsatz.
Das zeigte sich hier deutlich: Der Prototyp funktionierte technisch einwandfrei, wirkte aber wie ein trockenes IT-Werkzeug, dem zunächst kaum jemand seine Support-Fragen stellen wollte.
Rebranding als Strategie zur Steigerung der Chatbot-Nutzung
Den Durchbruch brachte am Ende ein Rebranding statt eines technischen Updates: Aus dem nüchternen „Hotline Agent“ wurde „Lumi“ – mit eigenem Namen, Avatar und einer internen Markenkampagne. Warum dieser Schritt so wichtig war und wie Architektur, Compliance-Leitplanken und Rebranding zusammenspielten, zeigt der vollständige Use Case.
Praxiseinblicke in die Architektur und Compliance von Lumi
In diesem t3n PRO Use Case liest du, wie Rewe digital aus einem technisch fertigen, aber ungenutzten Prototypen einen KI-Chatbot machte, der monatlich Tausende IT-Anfragen automatisiert löst:
- Einblick, wie das Rebranding die Nutzungszahlen in Schwung brachte
- Die Architektur dahinter – wie Lumi Treffer nach Relevanz filtert und externes Wissen ausschließt, um Halluzinationen zu vermeiden
- Einblick in die Compliance-Leitplanken, die Rewe digital gemeinsam mit dem Betriebsrat für den KI-Einsatz festgelegt hat

articles.title: a16z is challenging Silicon Valley's love for drop-outs by launching a school | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz is launching a school called The Horowitz Andreessen Academy aimed at aspiring founders who have just graduated high school and have not yet attended college.
The academy is aiming to train these high school grads with hands-on coursework on a variety of topics ranging from the technical (such as “AI Research and Models”) to life philosophy (such as “The Geometry of Luck,” which promises to teach students “about arranging a life so good fortune flows through it.”) Students will also work on personal projects. The school’s main pitch is that it promises to provide students with mentors who are big names in tech.
The school is currently accepting applications for its first year, which will be a one-year program that charges no tuition, and is open to about 50 students, “chosen on proof of work: what they have built, shipped, or earned,” according to the school’s FAQ. The academy is located in San Francisco and students will be responsible for their own housing (although the school is working to help them find it and match them with other student roommates).
One item to note: The academy is currently not an accredited school, so participants will not earn a degree, or college credits that transfer elsewhere.
In 2028, The Horowitz Andreessen Academy — which is a for-profit venture that has raised $42 million — hopes to offer a two-year program. At that point, it plans to charge tuition “similar in cost to an elite private university,” the school’s CEO Gagan Biyani said in a post on X. The schools, which is open to high school graduates, even if they are younger than 18, may also expand beyond 50 students in the future, an a16z spokesperson tells TechCrunch.
In exchange for that elite-tuition price tag, students will gain access to 200 speakers and mentors, including people from 10 founding corporate partners: Anduril, Anthropic, Coinbase, Google, Meta, Nvidia, OpenAI, Palantir, Replit, and Stripe. Those companies and dozens of others hope to hire from the grads of this school, Biyani said.
So, this is like if Y Combinator (the most famed startup school) and Peter Thiel’s Fellowship Program (a famed program for young people who opt to build companies instead of attend college) had a baby. The difference is, instead of a short-term experience ending with funding for a company, these students will pay tuition, earn tech-trade skills, and have an inside track at tech industry jobs. Or they may also have a startup in the works, built with access to a lot of mentorship.
As the founders of the academy describe, it’s meant to be a new, middle ground between obtaining a full degree before entering the tech industry and dropping out to start a company. In this era when AI has been hampering the entry-level job market, gaining access to jobs may be enough reason for some young people to try this new trade school-like approach.

articles.title: Ghana’s Complete Farmer secures $2.4m convertible loan from IFC - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Ghanaian agri-tech startup Complete Farmer has secured a US$2.4 million convertible loan from the International Finance Corporation (IFC) to scale up and finance inputs and agronomy services for farmers, complemented by US$480,000 in advisory to strengthen its systems and capacity to expand farmer financing.
Founded in 2017, Complete Farmer is an agricultural trading company connecting international commodity buyers with smallholder farmers across Ghana and Togo. The company works with more than 72,000 farmers and supplies international buyers, including Aldi and Lidl, and its operations are supported by more than 350 field agents and eight fulfillment centres responsible for aggregation, grading, quality control and export logistics.
The startup has expanded beyond agricultural trading, developing a marketplace for farm inputs and equipment and a credit product that uses farm data to help farmers access financing.
Complete Farmer raised US$10.4 million in pre-Series A funding back in September 2023, and last year banked US$2.5 million from the European Union-funded AgriFI facility to boost its expansion efforts. It has now secured further capital from the IFC, with support from the Business Investment Financing Track (BIFT) of the GAFSP, to help it connect more smallholder farmers with financial institutions. The partnership is expected to expand and provide support to 240,000 farmers, including facilitating access to finance by 2030.
“For us, this partnership is about making finance work better for farmers,” said Desmond Koney, CEO of Complete Farmer.
“Too many farmers with the capacity to grow commercially still struggle to access the financing they need to do so. Over the years, we have focused on building the technology, data and market infrastructure that makes it possible to better understand farmers, support their production and connect what they grow to real demand. Our partnership with IFC allows us to build on that foundation and scale our input financing model, so that more farmers have the resources and support they need to grow sustainably and participate more meaningfully in agricultural markets.”

articles.title: Proton signe avec Apertus pour une IA suisse souveraine
articles.text:
Proton ajoute Apertus 1.5 à son assistant Lumo. Ce modèle ouvert, conçu par l'ETH Zurich, l'EPFL et le CSCS, va désormais profiter des retours envoyés par les utilisateurs qui notent ses réponses.
Un modèle universitaire ne bénéficie pas des mêmes retombées qu'un modèle grand public utilisé par des millions de personnes chaque jour. Le partenariat annoncé entre les deux parties cherche justement à combler ce manque, sur la base du volontariat.
Comment vos retours sur Apertus atterrissent chez les chercheurs suisses
Apertus est un modèle entièrement ouvert. Ses poids sont publics. Il s'agit des valeurs numériques obtenues après l'entraînement, celles qui permettent de transformer une question en réponse. Ses données d'entraînement et ses méthodes le sont tout autant. Ses concepteurs affirment l'avoir entraîné uniquement sur des contenus accessibles publiquement. Ils disent aussi avoir respecté les demandes de retrait des ayants droit et filtré les informations personnelles. À son lancement en septembre 2025, nous présentions un modèle de 70 milliards de paramètres. Il était déjà entraîné sur plus de 1 000 langues et diffusé sous licence Apache 2.0.
Dans Lumo, Apertus 1.5 n'est pas activé par défaut. Il faut le sélectionner dans le menu déroulant des modèles, et on peut revenir à un autre modèle à tout moment. Les conversations restent protégées par le chiffrement zero-access, que seul l'appareil de l'utilisateur peut déchiffrer. Si aucune note n'est donnée, rien n'est transmis. En revanche, un pouce baissé sur une réponse envoie la question et la réponse concernées, de façon anonyme, aux chercheurs d'Apertus. Proton évoque plusieurs dizaines de millions d'utilisateurs de Lumo désormais en mesure de participer à cet effort, sur la base du volontariat.
Ce retour contient donc le texte que vous avez tapé. Mieux vaut éviter de noter négativement un échange contenant des informations personnelles si vous ne voulez pas qu'elles soient lues par d'autres personnes. Apertus convient surtout aux tâches courantes. Pour le raisonnement complexe, mieux vaut se tourner vers les autres modèles de Lumo. Qwen et GLM équipaient déjà la version 2.0 testée par nos soins. Du côté des chercheurs, Imanol Schlag, de l'ETH AI Center, y voit l'ingrédient qui manquait à un modèle entièrement ouvert et développé sur fonds publics.
Apertus n'est pas réservé à Proton. Euria, l'assistant d'Infomaniak que nous avons pris en main , le propose déjà sous l'étiquette "modèle suisse en développement", aux côtés de deux profils basés sur Qwen 3.5. La protection change cependant d'un service à l'autre. Euria mise sur un mode éphémère, quand Lumo chiffre les conversations sauvegardées. Pour Eamonn Maguire, directeur de l'IA chez Proton, une IA européenne ne suffit pas en soi. Elle doit rester compétitive pour être réellement utilisée.

articles.title: DataDome report finds bad bot traffic growing nine times faster than human traffic - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
DataDome report finds bad bot traffic growing nine times faster than human traffic
A new report out today from bot protection company DataDome SAS finds that malicious automated traffic grew 124% between July 2025 and June 2026, more than nine times the rate of human traffic growth — and most of the popular websites it tested could not stop a single bot.
The findings, from the 2026 edition of the company’s “State of Bot & Agent Security Report,” draw on more than a trillion requests across more than 75,000 customer sites, together with a June test of 21,491 popular websites. Scraping dominated the mix, at 70.9% of bad bot traffic and up 185.2% over the year. DataDome ties some of that growth to third-party data resellers and agent builders harvesting the web at scale for model training, activity that does not always identify itself as an artificial intelligence crawler.
Scalping, the use of bots to buy up limited inventory for resale, rose 290.7%, with median daily volume close to quadrupling, and fake account creation was up 34.5%. Distributed denial-of-service attacks grew 39.9% and peaked above 2 billion requests in a single day in April, which made them the second-largest category at 12.7% of bad bot traffic.
Credential stuffing was flat on the year. DataDome calls that pattern cyclical rather than fading, since volume surged through the summer of 2025, collapsed by nearly 90% and then reached new single-day highs by April.
AI traffic grew 82.3% over the same 12 months. DataDome logged 52.7 billion AI agent and crawler requests across its customer base, with Meta-affiliated bots generating 46.3% of the identified total and OpenAI-affiliated bots 34.6%. Of the 29.02 billion AI bot requests logged in the first half of 2026, 97.9% still went to homepages and other general content.
The other 2.1% is where the change shows up. AI agents sent 605.6 million requests to login, form, cart, payment and account-creation pages between January and June, and login pages took 51.7% of that, against 23% a year earlier. Monthly login-page volume from AI bots ran from 11.9 million requests in January to 99.7 million in June.
Jerome Segura, vice president of threat research at DataDome, said automated traffic is “growing fast” and moving into the login, account and transaction flows at the center of the customer journey. Identifying automation is not the hard part anymore, he said. The harder question is whether a given session is beneficial or harmful.
DataDome’s website test ran in June, sending 10 bot types at 21,491 sites across 15 industries from residential addresses in the U.S., Canada and France. Nearly two in three sites, 65.3%, stopped none of them, and the share reaching full protection has fallen two years running, to 2.4% from 8.4% in 2024, though this year’s test added harder bot types. Telecommunications sites were the weakest, at 82.9% unprotected.
Spoofed AI agents walked past more than seven sites in 10. DataDome calls identity-based trust a widespread weakness, since a request claiming to be GPTBot, ClaudeBot or another trusted crawler is often let through on the name alone. Only 5.5% of sites caught the test’s disguised bot, which forges the network fingerprint of a real browser.
Most of the defenses in use are “still largely built around binary choices,” Segura said, even as the calls organizations have to make get finer. The critical test, in his view, is whether a site can separate a legitimate AI assistant from a credential-testing bot or an account-abuse campaign. Blocking everything would also cut off beneficial activity, he added.

articles.title: Xbox préparerait une nouvelle vague de licenciements et un regroupement de ses studios
articles.text:
Mise à jour : La nouvelle vague de licenciements chez Xbox est désormais officielle. Dans un message envoyé ce 22 septembre aux employés de la division gaming de Microsoft, Matt Booty, responsable de Xbox Game Studios, annonce la suppression de 268 postes au sein de Halo Studios, d’autres studios first-party ainsi que des équipes de management.
En plus de ces licenciements, Xbox confirme une réorganisation de ses studios, avec l’objectif affiché de fonctionner avec moins d’unités, et de rapprocher des équipes qui travaillent déjà ensemble. La réorganisation concerne plusieurs studios de Xbox. Activision élargit son périmètre pour intégrer World’s Edge et Rare, et prendra également en charge le développement du prochain Halo, tandis qu’une petite équipe de Halo Studios continuera d’assurer le suivi des jeux existants et de la communauté.
Bethesda intégrera de son côté Obsidian, qui poursuivra ses projets actuels, dont le nouveau projet Fallout développé avec Bethesda Game Studios. King récupérera Microsoft Casual Games, tandis que Playground Games et Turn 10 seront réunis au sein d’un même studio consacré à Forza et Fable.
Xbox fait également le point sur les studios dont l’avenir avait été remis en question : Compulsion Games, Double Fine et désormais Undead Labs ont retrouvé leur indépendance. À l’inverse, Ninja Theory (Hellblade) fait face à une proposition de fermeture après l’échec de deux accords censés assurer son avenir, même si Xbox affirme chercher encore d’autres solutions, tandis que la consultation concernant Arkane se poursuit jusqu’à la fin de l’année.
Xbox Game Studios voit donc son périmètre fortement réduit, avec plusieurs studios fermés, cédés ou rattachés à Activision et Bethesda, passant d’une quinzaine de studios il y a trois ans à seulement quelques équipes directement rattachées au groupe.
Article publié initialement le 22 septembre 2026 : En juillet 2026, Microsoft avait annoncé une vague massive de licenciements, présentée par l’entreprise comme un « reset » de sa division Xbox. Cette nouvelle restructuration avait notamment entraîné la suppression de plusieurs milliers de postes et la fermeture ou l’annulation de plusieurs projets, illustrant l’ampleur du changement engagé au sein de la branche gaming du groupe.
Pour mesurer l’ampleur : le « reset » de juillet 2026 s’était traduit par environ 3 200 suppressions de postes, soit près de 20 % des effectifs de la division Xbox. Sur ce total, 1 600 postes avaient été supprimés immédiatement, les 1 600 autres devant s’étaler sur l’exercice fiscal 2027. Dans son mémo, la CEO Asha Sharma justifiait ce virage par des marges « 3 à 10 fois inférieures » à celles des concurrents.
Selon un article de The Information publié ce 22 septembre 2026 et relayé par Video Games Chronicle, Xbox préparerait déjà une nouvelle vague importante de licenciements. Plusieurs centaines de postes pourraient être supprimés cette semaine, tandis que Microsoft prévoirait également de consolider plusieurs de ses studios. Une source informée des projets du groupe explique que cette nouvelle réorganisation s’inscrit dans la volonté d’améliorer les marges de la division gaming et de concentrer davantage les investissements sur ses plus grandes franchises. Microsoft n’a pour l’instant pas confirmé ces nouvelles suppressions de postes.
Une nouvelle vague de licenciements et une consolidation des studios chez Xbox
Le terme de « consolidation » ne signifie toutefois pas nécessairement que les studios concernés vont fermer leurs portes. Il pourrait s’agir de regroupements et de changements dans l’organisation des différentes équipes de Microsoft. Aucun studio précis n’a été nommé par The Information, mais l’informateur NateTheHate affirme, ce 22 septembre, que certaines franchises et équipes pourraient changer de branche au sein du groupe. La franchise Halo serait notamment appelée à passer sous la responsabilité d’Activision Blizzard. Cette information ne signifie pas pour autant que Halo Studios disparaîtrait ou serait transféré, mais que la gestion de la franchise changerait de branche.
Cette réorganisation pourrait donc aller au-delà d’une simple réduction des effectifs, avec une nouvelle répartition des licences et des équipes entre Xbox Game Studios, Bethesda et Activision Blizzard. Microsoft n’a encore rien confirmé officiellement et n’a précisé, à ce stade, ni les équipes concernées ni le nombre exact d’emplois supprimés.

articles.title: Indian founders account for $560B unicorn valuation overseas: report
articles.text:
Indian founders account for $560B unicorn valuation overseas: report
The Diaspora Index by Prosus and Dealroom reveals the deep inroads by Indians founding companies overseas.
Founders who grew up in India account for $560 billion of founder-share-attributed company value in current and former unicorns abroad, according to the new Indian Diaspora Index from Prosus and Dealroom.
Based on the methodology used by the index, the value is an indicative figure and not based on actual shareholding of the individual founders.
"Founders who grew up in India account for $560 billion of founder-share-attributed company value in current and former unicorns abroad," the index report said.
To arrive at the valuation, the index took each company’s valuation and divided it equally among the founders, then counted the slice attributable to qualifying Indian-origin founders, regardless of their actual ownership.
"In contrast, 102 unicorns based in India account for approximately $349 billion on a founder-share basis, led by Flipkart ($36 billion), Zomato ($30 billion), and Groww ($16 billion)," the report said.
The Index showed that 70 unicorns worth $243 billion were built by all-Indian founders such as Jay Chaudhry (Zscaler), Arvind Jain, Arvind Nithrakashyap, Bipul Sinha and Soham Mazumdar (Rubrik), Ajeet Singh, Dheeraj Pandey and Mohit Aron (Nutanix), and Deepak Pathak and Abhinav Gupta (Skild).
Another 135 unicorns with Indian-origin founders in the core team, such as Palo Alto, Bloom Energy, Astera Labs and Perplexity, contributed $317 billion on this founder-share basis.
Prosus India Principal Investor Saurav Jain said that Indian founders have the ability to turn technology, ingenuity and deep local insight into businesses that can fundamentally change how people live and work.
"Indian Diaspora Index measures something we have seen and experienced first-hand in India: exceptional talent density with the ambition to build at enormous scale, often by solving some of the country's most complex and consequential problems. That is what has kept us investing in the country for nearly two decades," he said.
The report said that a separate, broader birth-origin analysis shows that 62 per cent of its companies are based in the United States, making it the dominant ecosystem for Indian-origin founders building high-value companies.
"In total, 200 of the 323 companies in this broader cohort were either started (178) or relocated (22) to the United States. This birth-origin analysis includes founders who left India as children and companies based in India. It is separate from the narrower overseas index of founders who grew up in India," the report said.

articles.title: À 6 000 mètres sous l'océan, ces robots révèlent ce que personne n'avait encore pu observer
articles.text:
Plus de 70 % de notre planète est recouverte par les océans, mais la majeure partie reste un angle mort pour les scientifiques. Si le programme international Argo déploie déjà 4 000 flotteurs à travers le globe, la grande majorité d’entre eux se limite à des profondeurs comprises entre 2 000 et 4 000 mètres. Or, environ 10 % du réchauffement total des océans se produit sous le seuil des 2 000 mètres, créant un manque important de données. Pour combler cette lacune, l’Ifremer a fait plonger ses prototypes baptisés Deep-6000.
Des abysses sous haute surveillance
Entre le 11 janvier et le 2 février, les deux prototypes français ont réalisé cinq cycles complets de plongée à 6 000 mètres de profondeur au nord des Antilles. Ces missions permettent à la France de rejoindre le cercle très fermé des pays capables de concevoir des profileurs Argo pour ces profondeurs extrêmes, derrière les États-Unis et la Chine. D’ici 2028, une flotte de trente de ces machines rejoindra le réseau mondial pour couvrir plus de 98 % du volume océanique.
Chaque appareil fonctionne selon un cycle bien rodé de dix jours. Largué depuis un bateau, il descend en profondeur, dérive pendant neuf jours, mesure les données pendant trois heures lors de sa phase de profil, puis remonte à la surface pour transmettre ses relevés par satellite. Ces engins mesurent en temps réel la température, la salinité, l’oxygène et la pression de l’eau. Ces précieuses informations permettront aux climatologues de suivre la propagation de la chaleur et du carbone stockés dans les grands fonds, d’affiner les modèles de prévision et de mieux comprendre l’impact sur la montée du niveau de la mer.
À lire : Fin de l’ISS : la NASA veut jeter la station dans l’océan, les écologistes s’insurgent
Un défi d’ingénierie face à la pression extrême
Concevoir un robot capable de résister à la pression colossale des abysses (environ 600 fois la pression de surface à 6 000 mètres) a nécessité de faire certains choix techniques. L’équipe de développement de l’Ifremer, basée à Plouzané dans le Finistère, a privilégié un matériau composite plutôt que le titane pur pour façonner les coques des flotteurs. Ainsi, chaque appareil pèse environ 40 kg, soit le double d’un flotteur Argo classique, pour garantir sa robustesse sous l’eau.
« Le principal défi consistait à concevoir un système capable de résister aux pressions des grands fonds marins, d’être autonome en énergie pour rester
 opérationnel pendant sept ans et de maîtriser les coûts », explique Xavier André, responsable du développement technologique des profileurs à l’Ifremer.
La fabrication en série de ces prototypes sera assurée par nke Instrumentation à Hennebont (dans l’ouest du Morbihan), tandis que le superordinateur Datarmor de l’Ifremer stockera les précieuses données récoltées. L’objectif affiché est de maintenir ces équipements opérationnels pendant sept ans malgré des conditions d’utilisation d’une rudesse extrême.

articles.title: Cyera Raises $400 Million at $12+ Billion Valuation
articles.text:
Data security company Cyera has received an additional $400 million in funding, bringing the company’s valuation to more than $12 billion.
The new investment came from Goldman Sachs Alternatives as an extension of the Series G funding round announced in June. The company has raised a total of more than $2.7 billion.
The latest funding will be used to continue enhancing the Cyera platform’s capabilities and fuel the company’s expansion and growth.
Cyera provides an agentless, API-driven data security platform designed to deliver real-time visibility and context-aware governance over sensitive information across hybrid cloud, SaaS, database, and on-premises environments.
The platform continuously scans structured and unstructured data stores to build a unified inventory, leveraging ML to classify data by business context and compliance requirements.
Cyera unifies Data Security Posture Management (DSPM), Data Loss Prevention (DLP), and identity access governance. By continuously correlating data sensitivity with user identity permissions, it can discover security misconfigurations, over-permissioned access, and high-risk sharing.
The platform also provides guardrails for AI operations, monitoring data inputs to LLMs, inspecting training datasets, and mitigating exfiltration risks across automated AI workflows.
“Cyera was the first to bring data and identity together, and as [AI] agents multiply faster than anyone can track, the gap between what they’re trusted to do and what they can actually reach is becoming increasingly dangerous. Cyera’s technology, customer traction, and execution position it to become the platform enterprises rely on to secure AI,” said Irit Kahan, managing director within Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives.
In late July, Cyera announced the acquisition of agentic access management provider Oasis Security in a $1 billion deal.
Cyera says it has over 1,500 employees and claims its solutions are used by 20% of Fortune 500 companies.

articles.title: New ClosedQuorum Windows malware uses AI for attack decisions
articles.text:
A new Windows malware named ClosedQuorum uses Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, and Mistral AI models to autonomously determine the actions to take during post-compromise stages of an attack.
The Go-based malware acts with no commands from a human operator, using reconnaissance information and a voting system to decide its next step on infected hosts.
When votes are tied, DeepSeek has priority at making the final call, based on the option it considers most appropriate, followed by Qwen, Mistral, and Gemini.
Cisco Talos researchers analyzing ClosedQuorum say that the models are restricted to a predefined set of decisions, including:
- steal — simultaneously runs LSASS credential dumping, browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox) credential theft, and cryptocurrency-wallet (MetaMast, Exodus, Ethereum) extraction
- inject — generates shellcode, then uses either process hollowing or Early Bird APC injection
- persist — executes the malware’s persistence module
- move — included as a possible lateral movement decision, but the analyzed distribution build has no corresponding handler, so it cannot execute this action
The stolen details are then passed to the operators via a Discord webhook, so apart from the malware delivery, the attack can be fully automated.
Talos describes ClosedQuorum as the first publicly documented Windows implant to delegate tactical command-and-control (C2) decisions to a panel of AI models, commenting that this adds greater speed and scaling potential to malicious operations.
The researchers also highlight that this eliminates human interaction, allowing the attack chain to proceed at any time.
However, Cisco notes that this may also pose challenges in certain cases where rate limits are hit, output is malformed, or commercial APIs that the system relies on are temporarily unavailable.
Since it is not a sophisticated piece of malware, it is unclear if ClosedQuorum is a test or experiment. However, the researchers warn that it represents an "architectural shift towards attack-chain automation."
“While we do not have confirmation of in-the-wild deployment, artifacts from the binary were used to connect the developer to postings on criminal forums related to carding, dating back to 2025,” explains Cisco Talos.
The binary that Cisco Talos analyzed contains placeholder API credentials and a dummy Discord webhook, although the creators can add those in their custom ClosedQuorum builds.
Cisco Talos discovered ClosedQuorum through CAIRN, an open-source toolkit it released to help researchers track and analyze AI-integrated malware.

articles.title: Lista de códigos de Free Fire para reclamar premios y diamantes este 22 de septiembre de 2026
articles.text:
Los jugadores de Free Fire pueden probar una nueva lista de códigos de canje este 22 de septiembre de 2026, con la posibilidad de obtener diamantes, aspectos visuales, trajes, cajas de botín y otros objetos para usar dentro del videojuego.
Las combinaciones deben ingresarse en el portal oficial de recompensas de Garena antes de que pierdan vigencia. Por ese motivo, los usuarios deben realizar el procedimiento cuanto antes y verificar el resultado dentro de su cuenta.
PUBLICIDAD
Cuáles códigos está disponibles para redimir en Free Fire
Los códigos se componen de letras y números, así que deben copiarse con precisión y respetar las mayúsculas. Cada combinación puede dejar de funcionar sin previo aviso si alcanzó el máximo de canjes permitido o si no está habilitada para el país asociado a la cuenta. Los códigos son:
- P3LX6V9TM2QH.
- FFWCTKX2P5NQ.
- TX4SC2VUNPKF.
- RHTG9VOLTDWP.
- N7QK5L3MRP9J.
- J2QP8M1KVL6V.
- E9QH6K4LNP7V.
- S5PL7M2LRV8K.
- Q8M4K7L2VR9J.
- RD3TZK7WME65.
- ZRW3J4N8VX56.
- TFX9J3Z2RP64.
- WD2ATK3ZEA55.
- FFPLUFBVSLOT.
- MCPW3D28VZD6.
- ZZZ76NT3PDSH.
- V427K98RUCHZ.
De qué forma canjear los códigos en el portal oficial de Garena
El proceso se realiza en el sitio de recompensas de Garena, disponible en reward.ff.garena.com. El usuario debe ingresar con la misma cuenta que usa en Free Fire, porque el sistema deposita los objetos en el inventario asociado a ese perfil.
La app habilita el acceso mediante Google, Facebook, Apple, Huawei o VK. Tras iniciar sesión, hay que pegar uno de los códigos en el campo de canje y confirmar la operación. Si el sistema acepta la combinación, el premio llegará al correo interno del juego, desde donde podrá redimirse.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué recompensas pueden entregar los códigos de Free Fire
Los códigos promocionales suelen incluir artículos virtuales de distinto tipo. Entre los más buscados aparecen los diamantes, una moneda del juego que permite acceder a contenido adicional, participar de ciertas opciones de la tienda y desbloquear objetos disponibles por tiempo limitado.
La recompensa final depende del código validado y puede variar incluso entre usuarios registrados. Garena distribuye trajes, skins de armas, accesorios, emotes, cajas de botín y artículos coleccionables. No todas las combinaciones entregan diamantes, así que conviene revisar el correo interno luego de completar el canje.
Por qué algunos códigos aparecen como vencidos o no son válidos para canjear
Un mensaje de error no siempre significa que el proceso se haya realizado de forma incorrecta. Los códigos cuentan con una cantidad limitada de usos y pueden agotarse en pocas horas, sobre todo cuando circulan entre una gran cantidad de jugadores. Hay combinaciones que solo funcionan en determinados territorios.
PUBLICIDAD
La fecha de expiración es otro de los motivos habituales. Los códigos de Free Fire no permanecen activos de forma indefinida y Garena puede deshabilitarlos cuando concluye una campaña, un evento o una distribución específica. Si una clave no funciona, la alternativa es probar con otra de la lista sin modificar sus caracteres.
Cuáles son los requisitos para reclamar recompensas en Free Fire
El canje está reservado para cuentas registradas y vinculadas a uno de los servicios de acceso permitidos. Las cuentas de invitado no pueden utilizar el portal de recompensas, porque no disponen de una vinculación que permita identificar el inventario al que deben enviarse los objetos.
Asimismo, quienes jueguen como invitados deberán asociar su perfil a Google, Facebook, Apple, Huawei o VK antes de intentar el proceso. Se sugiere descargar Free Fire solo desde Google Play Store o App Store.
PUBLICIDAD
Las versiones modificadas y las páginas que prometen diamantes ilimitados pueden solicitar claves, datos bancarios o descargas externas. El único canal habilitado para reclamar los códigos es el portal oficial de Garena.
Los usuarios deben mantener actualizados sus dispositivos para evitar perder acceso a las novedades de diferentes aplicaciones.
